title: From Retouched Images to Paired Videos: A Synthetic Benchmark for Face Video Retouching

payload.title: From Retouched Images to Paired Videos: A Synthetic Benchmark for Face Video Retouching
payload.abstract: Paired unretouched/retouched face videos are costly to produce because professional editing must remain consistent over time, while releasing identifiable face footage raises privacy, consent, and governance concerns. We present DeepVFR, an initial controlled synthetic benchmark-not a new retouching architecture-for paired face video retouching. Starting from paired synthetic DeepFRR images, Wan2.2 generates mild-motion source clips, and backend-specific face transfer constructs synchronized proxy retouching targets, followed by automatic validity screening and manual visual inspection. DeepVFR contains 1,024 pairs of 150-frame clips at 30 fps, evaluated under an identity-disjoint protocol with explicit frame correspondence; release metadata will record the construction route. Within-benchmark baselines, external checkpoints applied to DeepVFR, qualitative analysis, and a 17-participant ranking study establish reference behavior in the controlled domain. The constructed targets exhibit a substantial low-preference tail in the human study. Because both streams inherit synthetic content and the targets additionally inherit commercial-API or face-transfer artifacts, the benchmark neither replaces artist-retouched captured video nor establishes synthetic-to-real generalization. DeepVFR provides a starting point for paired supervision and controlled evaluation. Data, individual study rankings, and training logs will be made publicly available upon acceptance. Broader motion coverage and real-video validation remain future work.

title: Setting Optimal Reserve Prices using Fine-Tuned Language Models

payload.title: Setting Optimal Reserve Prices using Fine-Tuned Language Models
payload.abstract: Online auction houses must set reserve prices for highly differentiated products whose unstructured descriptions contain valuable demand information. Existing approaches generally require managers to specify product attributes in advance. We ask whether a language model can instead learn from listing descriptions and historical bids to set item-specific reserve prices before bidding begins. We fine-tune a pretrained text embedding language model using the structural likelihood of auction bids as its training objective. This directs representation learning toward the valuation distribution that determines the reserve decision. We show that consecutive upper bids identify the tail information needed to set an optimal reserve without observing or modeling the number of potential bidders. A split-sample estimator learns the representation on one half of the data and conducts structural estimation and inference conditional on that representation on the other. We apply the method to approximately 65,800 online used-vehicle auctions. With seller values calibrated to match the sale rate among listings, the model implies a counterfactual net increase of $165.8 million, representing a 14.6% increase above the incumbent reserve policy. The framework translates a listing description and a seller's value into an item-specific reserve recommendation without constructing a product taxonomy or requiring a bid history for the item being priced. It provides an approach to adapting language models for operational decisions in marketplaces where products are heterogeneous and demand-relevant information is recorded in text.

title: Third-Place Solution for the UCF UrbanTwin V2X-Real Track at ECCV 2026: Synthetic Point Cloud Generation and Sim-to-Real 3D Object Detection

payload.title: Third-Place Solution for the UCF UrbanTwin V2X-Real Track at ECCV 2026: Synthetic Point Cloud Generation and Sim-to-Real 3D Object Detection
payload.abstract: This report presents a complete technical solution for the UrbanTwin V2X-Real Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, covering both synthetic point cloud generation and 3D object detection. For data generation, we adopt per-axis quantile calibration. Public V2X-Real training data are used to construct the real reference distribution, and independent one-dimensional quantile mappings are estimated for the x, y, and z axes of the base synthetic point clouds. The calibrated point clouds are then resampled using a fixed random seed and clipped to the valid spatial range, producing 50 frames with 2,000 float32 XYZ points per frame. For detection, we use a two-stage Voxel R-CNN (VoxelRCNN) detector trained with RangeLDM-enhanced synthetic point-cloud data, point clouds downsampled to 50k points per frame, and reconstructed pedestrian data. Training is performed on four NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPUs with a global batch size of 16 for 40 epochs. Final testing uses direct single-model inference with the original VoxelRCNN model. On the official evaluation server, the normalized Realism score is 0.7905 and the normalized Detection score is 0.5583, with mAP@0.5 of 0.3908, BEV mAP@0.5 of 0.4219, and mAP@0.7 of 0.1047. According to the official weighting rule, the final combined score is 0.6 x 0.5583 + 0.4 x 0.7905 = 0.6512. This report documents the complete implementation details of data construction, model training, inference, submission formatting, and official evaluation.

title: Vibe synthesis: hierarchical agentic decision-making for intent-driven multistep molecule synthesis

payload.title: Vibe synthesis: hierarchical agentic decision-making for intent-driven multistep molecule synthesis
payload.abstract: The ability to construct complex molecules underpins advances in medicine and the molecular sciences. Yet long-horizon multistep synthesis requires decisions to be revised as evidence accumulates across chemically dependent operations, a capability not readily supported by artificial-intelligence tools and automated platforms organized around predefined tasks and hard-coded workflows. Here we propose and demonstrate a vibe synthesis system (VibeSyn), an intent-driven architecture in which hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined molecular objectives and accumulating evidence into adaptive decisions executed through computational tools and laboratory automation. We evaluate VibeSyn in three demonstrations of increasing scope and autonomy, progressing from evidence-grounded experimental decisions to adaptive execution of a ten-step total synthesis of catharanthine and structure-to-compound synthesis of cyclic peptides containing unnatural amino acids (uAAs). Across the long-horizon campaigns, active human input and simple confirmation account for less than 7.5% and 5.2%, respectively, of recorded workflow actions and outcomes. VibeSyn points towards a future in which chemists define synthetic intent and agent-directed laboratories autonomously navigate the evolving experimental trajectory required to deliver the target compound.

title: Agri-MRAG: Parameter-Enhanced Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Agricultural Visual Question Answering

payload.title: Agri-MRAG: Parameter-Enhanced Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Agricultural Visual Question Answering
payload.abstract: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) has shown promise for Agricultural Visual Question Answering (Agri-VQA), but existing methods still face challenges in retrieving relevant knowledge while avoiding redundancy and in integrating retrieved evidence beyond simple prompt concatenation. To address these issues, we propose Agri-MRAG, a multimodal retrieval-augmented framework for agricultural VQA. Specifically, we first introduce a semantic-consistency-guided clustering mechanism that combines multimodal clustering and weighted relevance scoring to select high-confidence knowledge subsets and adaptively determine the retrieval size $k$. We then design a parameterized knowledge injection strategy, where retrieved agricultural knowledge is encoded into LoRA adapters and merged into the feed-forward network (FFN) layers of the MLLM, allowing external knowledge to influence generation through parameter-level adaptation. In addition, a perplexity-guided (PPL-guided) routing mechanism is employed to switch between implicit parametric reasoning and explicit retrieval-assisted generation according to model uncertainty, balancing inference efficiency and answer reliability. For evaluation, we use PlantVillageVQA as a broad agricultural benchmark and construct PlantVQA, a region-specific forestry and fruit crop VQA dataset containing 7,514 images and 15,028 expert-verified question-answer pairs. Experiments show that Agri-MRAG achieves ROUGE-L scores of 41.21 and 46.58 on the two datasets, outperforming mRAG by 11.70 and 4.51 points, and VisRAG by 8.80 and 3.39 points, respectively.

title: AerialOcc: Unified 3D Aerial Perception without Task-Specific Head

payload.title: AerialOcc: Unified 3D Aerial Perception without Task-Specific Head
payload.abstract: Aerial perception systems are increasingly expected to support diverse tasks, yet existing solutions remain fundamentally tied to task-specific outputs. Detection, segmentation, and other perception objectives are usually learned either by separate models or by sharing a backbone with multiple task heads, leaving the model itself unaware of the common structure underlying these tasks. We are interested in asking: can a single perception representation support different levels of understanding without being designed for any specific task? We notice that occupancy is a promising task-agnostic representation for drone perception. By modeling the spatial existence and semantics of the environment, it naturally bridges different perception granularities, from coarse scene understanding to fine-grained object localization. Therefore, we introduce AerialOcc, a unified occupancy-based perception model that enables multiple drone perception tasks from a single inference process, without maintaining task-specific prediction heads. To facilitate this direction, we construct AerialOcc-20K, a large-scale multi-class occupancy dataset for aerial environments. Extensive experiments show that AerialOcc achieves competitive performance across diverse perception tasks while preserving a unified architecture. Our findings demonstrate that occupancy can serve as a universal perception interface, offering a new perspective toward flexible and scalable visual intelligence for autonomous drones from a common 3D scene representation. Models and data are publicly available at https://github.com/guxiang2002/AerialOcc

title: Gradient-Guided Hardware-Native MIXFP4

payload.title: Gradient-Guided Hardware-Native MIXFP4
payload.abstract: Blackwell tensor cores support native inference with 4-bit weights and activations (W4A4), but NVFP4 leaves a perplexity (PPL) gap to BF16. Choosing a format for each 16-element block can improve accuracy, but current matrix multiply instructions cannot execute choices this fine. Applying these rules at hardware-compatible tiles loses most of their benefit. We introduce FlipQuant, which selects E2M1 or E0M3 for each MMA weight tile. It keeps both quantized weight candidates fixed and learns a binary format map from end-to-end gradients of a bucketed KL loss to a BF16 teacher, re-evaluating them after each update. Native kernels execute 16 x 64 tiles on SM120 and 256 x 64 tiles on SM100 with median GEMM overheads of 1.9% and 1.7%, respectively. Across six language models and two corpora, FlipQuant at 16 x 64 closes 42.5% of NVFP4's PPL gap to BF16 on average, compared with 13.3% for FourOverSix. Code is available at https://github.com/brian030128/flipquant.

title: Frame First, Decode Once: Object-Centric Coordinates and Single-Pass Decoding for System-1 World Models

payload.title: Frame First, Decode Once: Object-Centric Coordinates and Single-Pass Decoding for System-1 World Models
payload.abstract: Single-pass primitive decoders such as LocateAnything and VFlash predict all quantized coordinate tokens of a geometric primitive in one forward pass, enabling fast, System-1 visual planning. We study what matters when such a decoder serves as a System-1 world model: a fast action-conditioned predictor that ranks candidate pushes by their predicted outcome. On ManiSkill3 PushT-v1 (512 held-out test families, 8,192 rollouts) and on human demonstrations from lerobot/pusht (2,384 test windows), we compare decoders, training losses, rigid-body projections and coordinate frames, using matched checkpoints, hierarchical bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm correction. Two factors of similar size dominate. First, expressing inputs and outputs in the SE(2) frame of the object's initial pose lowers decision regret by 1.9-2.2x for each of five decoders, and the object-frame model trained on 128 families matches the world-frame model trained on 512. Second, single-pass decoding outperforms iterative decoding: in the object frame, single-pass heads reach 0.020-0.021 regret at 1.6-1.8 ms per decision, against 0.046 for 10-step DDIM diffusion and 0.059 for KV-cached autoregression at 10.3 and 12.9 ms. The choice among single-pass heads has no measurable effect on regret, and our registered hypothesis that the frame effect exceeds the decoder spread is not supported. Soft-token expectation with an end-to-end 2D Kabsch projection gives the lowest trajectory error (11.35 px on ManiSkill3, 3.78 px on lerobot/pusht), exact rigid-body consistency, and lower regret than diffusion at every budget from 4 to 50 DDIM steps, at 3-29x lower latency.

title: From Hosted Service to Field-Owned Infrastructure: Open, Self-Hosted Real-Time Camera-Trap Alerting with Regional Open-Weight Models

payload.title: From Hosted Service to Field-Owned Infrastructure: Open, Self-Hosted Real-Time Camera-Trap Alerting with Regional Open-Weight Models
payload.abstract: Cellular camera traps can alert field teams within minutes, supporting anti-poaching, threatened-species protection and human-wildlife conflict mitigation. Most systems use central servers, sending images of people and sensitive species locations outside the collecting organisation and often across national borders. We ask whether this capability can run on infrastructure owned by field organisations. Trap Tracker RT is an open-source, self-hosted application that receives images by email or locally via FTP/SFTP, classifies them with a project-specific model and sends alerts through a mail server chosen by the organisation. We evaluated DeepFaune-SSA v1.2, pairing MegaDetector v6 with a DINOv3-based classifier for 33 sub-Saharan taxa, against three open alternatives on 31,131 out-of-distribution images from Kenya, Namibia and Malawi, independent of its training data. DeepFaune-SSA achieved image-level species accuracy of 0.901 (95% CI 0.894-0.908), versus 0.530 for the global SpeciesNet classifier and 0.556 and 0.547 for YOLOv10x and YOLO26x detectors trained on the same regional data. DeepFaune-SSA had the highest recall for all 26 species evaluated. The single-stage detectors missed animals in about a quarter of images; SpeciesNet assigned species labels in only 57%, usually falling back to coarser labels otherwise. In bench tests of the fully local path, alerts were issued about 6 s after upload completion, including with slowed and interrupted uploads. The two-stage pipeline processed 19 images per minute on eight CPU threads without a graphics processor. Trap Tracker RT is used by five organisations in the United Kingdom and Kenya, including for human-elephant conflict mitigation. We discuss how data paths, rather than inference location, determine data sovereignty, the responsibilities of self-hosting and the ethics of real-time monitoring.

title: VTG-RAG: Long-Video Reasoning via Query-Adaptive Coarse-to-Fine Sampling and Temporal Graph Retrieval

payload.title: VTG-RAG: Long-Video Reasoning via Query-Adaptive Coarse-to-Fine Sampling and Temporal Graph Retrieval
payload.abstract: Long-video reasoning requires a system to localize sparse evidence over extended temporal sequences, preserve temporal structure, and generate answers despite substantial multimodal distractors. Existing video retrieval-augmented generation methods typically build indexes from uniformly sampled video segments. In long-video settings, this design readily introduces irrelevant context and is unreliable for questions with explicit temporal constraints. We propose VTG-RAG, a framework for long-video question answering that combines query-adaptive coarse-to-fine sampling with temporal graph retrieval. First, a two-stage sampling strategy selects core segments with high mean query relevance or high intra-segment relevance variance. The framework then integrates subtitles, speech transcripts, visual descriptions, entities, and relations from these segments into a temporally ordered multimodal graph. Finally, it performs temporally filtered, two-pass retrieval and reasoning across frame, text, and graph evidence spaces. A lot of experiments have proven the effectiveness of the VTG-RAG. Specifically, we evaluate the framework on Video-MME and LongVideoBench. On LongVideoBench, the reported Qwen2.5-VL-32B and 72B results improve from 48.16% to 50.56% and from 52.13% to 53.32%, respectively, with 24 answer-input frames. These correspond to gains of 2.40 and 1.19 percentage points. The ablation experiments of VTG-RAG further support that the contributions of each component are very important.

title: Target-Free Autocalibration of Stereo PIV Camera Systems via Persistent-State Motion Representations

payload.title: Target-Free Autocalibration of Stereo PIV Camera Systems via Persistent-State Motion Representations
payload.abstract: Stereo Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) recovers three-component velocity fields by triangulating tracer particles observed by synchronized cameras. It requires an accurate extrinsic calibration, which is still obtained by inserting a physical target into the flow and must be repeated whenever the rig is moved. We present a target-free method that calibrates a stereo PIV rig directly from particle image sequences. Because tracer particles are visually indistinguishable, we match motion rather than appearance: building on CUT3R, each camera stream is processed by a recurrent transformer whose persistent state accumulates particle motion over time. The state is decoded into per-camera optical flow and queried by a cross-view decoder that regresses bidirectional point correspondences, from which the relative pose is recovered with a five-point RANSAC solver. We train on a new synthetic stereo PIV dataset with ground-truth poses and evaluate on standard PIV optical flow benchmarks and on 200 real rig placements. Our model achieves lower flow error than existing PIV networks, more accurate cross-view correspondences than COTR, and higher pose accuracy than the strongest detector-matcher pipelines on both synthetic and real data, without any calibration target.

title: TyphoonWorld: A Residual Token World Model for Probabilistic Forecasting of Typhoon Imagery

payload.title: TyphoonWorld: A Residual Token World Model for Probabilistic Forecasting of Typhoon Imagery
payload.abstract: A satellite forecast of a typhoon should give a low-error picture of the next two days, together with an ensemble whose members are coherent fields and whose spread responds to the storm at hand. A small direct regression network already gives the lowest squared error on held-out storms, so a generative model has to earn its cost through the part of the future that the regression smooths away. We present TyphoonWorld, a discrete-token world model that generates only that part. Conditioned on tokens of the regression forecast, the latest frames and the best-track state at forecast time, it samples residual fields lead by lead, and members add these residuals to the regression center. We compare it under one protocol with per-pixel Gaussian networks, a diffusion model of the same residuals, residuals from other storms and an unconditional token world model, on 276 forecast windows from 46 held-out storms of Digital Typhoon. TyphoonWorld matches the squared error of the regression, lowers the CRPS of the area colder than 220 K, a direct measure of deep convection, by 14 to 39% against every other ensemble, and ties its spread to forecast error as closely as the Gaussian network, with a correlation of 0.78 across windows. It uses 56% of the parameters of the unconditional world model.

title: LiNO: Lightweight Network for Occupancy Estimation

payload.title: LiNO: Lightweight Network for Occupancy Estimation
payload.abstract: Occupancy estimation for automated vehicles is a crucial task that builds a 3D map using vehicle sensors. This map allows the vehicle to identify drivable areas and various obstacle classes. The task involves complex subtasks such as depth estimation, object classification, and segmentation to align semantic information with the 3D grid. Moreover, producing these estimations from multiple sensors demands significant computational power and memory, as high-dimensional data fusion requires complex feature extraction and processing. Consequently, most existing methods rely on large and computationally intensive architectures that are not suitable for real-time or real-world applications. We present a real-time, lightweight architecture that leverages camera and radar sensors through a residual multi-stage head. Unlike prior methods that rely on heavy camera-only blocks, our architecture employs camera-radar fusion and lightweight components. Additionally, we introduce a task-specific data augmentation strategy that enhances data diversity and improves generalisation. Our method achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, attaining 45.7 mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) on Occ3D and 41.9 Ray-level Intersection over Union (RayIoU) (41.9) on OpenOcc datasets, running at 17.2 frames per second (FPS) and using only 5.3 GB of memory, compared with 4.1 FPS and 7.7 GB for STCOcc.

title: Wrong with Confidence: Measuring Hallucination, Overconfidence and Identity-Conditioned Behaviour in Large Language Models

payload.title: Wrong with Confidence: Measuring Hallucination, Overconfidence and Identity-Conditioned Behaviour in Large Language Models
payload.abstract: Large language models answer underspecified questions readily, and accuracy-only evaluation rewards guessing over abstaining. Observational studies link query underspecification to hallucination, but they cannot separate the effect of missing information from item difficulty, and they rarely ask what the model tells the user. We report a pre-registered, paired behavioural study of five open-weight models (Gemma 3 27B, Gemma 4 31B, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B and Nemotron 3 Super). Each of 142 factual questions was posed in a fully specified form and in a referentially underspecified form with the same answer key, and three probes measured identity-conditioned behaviour. Two raters scored 5,620 responses under a fixed rubric; effects were estimated with mixed-effects models. Without the referent, the models sought clarification on 33.7% of prompts and answered the rest. Among attempted answers, the error rate rose from 39.1% to 52.0% (mixed-effects odds ratio 4.12, 95% CI 2.76-6.14), and specialist-domain questions failed more often than general ones in every model. Unelicited verbal uncertainty did not track this risk: 75.3% of wrong answers carried no hedge, wrong answers to underspecified prompts were hedged no more often than wrong answers to clear prompts (27.3% vs 22.3%), and hedging separated correct from incorrect answers only weakly (AUROC 0.56). Gendered pronouns followed occupational stereotypes whenever a model committed to one; any stated user identity lengthened answers by about 45% relative to an anonymous user; claimed expertise did not reduce safety caveats. The models either ask or answer as if the question were well posed, and the wording of a guess does not reveal that it is one. Evaluations should score clarification as a distinct outcome and check label validity as well as rater agreement.

title: Detection Is Not the Finish Line: Multiscale Decoding and Constraint-Aware Global Association for Multi-Camera 3D Tracking

payload.title: Detection Is Not the Finish Line: Multiscale Decoding and Constraint-Aware Global Association for Multi-Camera 3D Tracking
payload.abstract: A query-based multi-view 3D detector can transfer well to a new calibrated camera network and still produce badly fragmented tracks: on the AI City Challenge 2026 Track 1 validation set, the frozen Sparse4D detector behind the official challenge winner splits each Person identity into a median of eight fragments, and half of the gaps between fragments exceed the horizon of a causal tracker. We show that most of the remaining headroom of such a system lies after detection. Keeping the public detector frozen, we add (i) class-wise source selection between two input scales, which recovers small and distant people from a 0.75x pass while leaving large objects at the scale the detector was trained for; (ii) a geometry-to-appearance bridge that projects every 3D box into all calibrated views, matches it to 2D person detections, and aggregates robust track-level re-identification descriptors; and (iii) constraint-aware consolidation, which combines a causal short-gap stitch with offline centroid-linkage clustering under two hard constraints, temporal exclusion and metric 3D reachability, plus class-aware long-gap stitching for rigid objects. Every association stage changes object identities only. On the challenge evaluation server the system scores 62.3947 3D HOTA (DetA 57.4501, AssA 56.8131, LocA 80.1272), first on the general leaderboard snapshot of 30 October 2026 (second at the time of writing, after a competitor's detector update) and 5.63 points above our reproduction of the official winner; the constrained association stage alone contributes +3.73 HOTA through a +5.49 AssA gain at unchanged DetA. Controlled fixed-box validation studies, a constraint ablation, sensitivity curves, and a catalogue of negative results support the design.

title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement

payload.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
payload.abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

title: LVRE: A Local Visual Reasoning and Editing Agent for Optical Chemical Structure Recognition

payload.title: LVRE: A Local Visual Reasoning and Editing Agent for Optical Chemical Structure Recognition
payload.abstract: Optical chemical structure recognition (OCSR) demands strict all-or-nothing graph fidelity, where a single misidentified bond order or formal charge makes the predicted graph differ from the reference structure. While vision-language models (VLMs) can reinspect ambiguous visual regions, unconstrained full-graph regeneration often introduces regressive errors into previously correct substructures. We present LVRE, a training-free visual agent that refines molecular graphs via targeted visual inspection and reversible transactional editing. Rather than regenerating the entire graph sequence, LVRE examines a high-resolution crop alongside the global diagram and local graph neighborhood, proposing modifications to named graph records that a deterministic controller checks. A controller executes each proposed modification as an isolated transaction, and a visual review module arbitrates which edits to commit or roll back. Across four foundation VLMs, LVRE improves graph accuracy by 8.0-8.5 percentage points over single-pass recognition and by 3.0-3.3 points over fixed local review. In a paired evaluation of 1,000 diagrams using Gemini 3.8 Flash, LVRE achieves 100 successful repairs while introducing only 15 regressive errors, in contrast to global reflection which yields 65 repairs against 30 introduced errors. On this paired set, LVRE introduces half as many errors on initially correct predictions as global reflection.

title: T2T Technical Report: Synthesizing GUI Agent Trajectories at Scale from Video Tutorials

payload.title: T2T Technical Report: Synthesizing GUI Agent Trajectories at Scale from Video Tutorials
payload.abstract: Training generalist GUI agents requires large volumes of interaction trajectories comprising screenshot sequences paired with grounded UI actions, yet collecting such data through human demonstration is expensive and difficult to scale. Although public software tutorial videos contain rich operational demonstrations, their continuous pixel streams lack discrete action boundaries, semantic intents, and precise spatial coordinates, making them difficult to use directly for model training. To address this, we present T2T (Tutorial-to-Trajectory), a fully automated pipeline for synthesizing GUI agent trajectories at scale. T2T spans desktop, web, and mobile platforms to convert unannotated video tutorials into structured, executable interaction trajectories. To guarantee trajectory quality, T2T combines active segment filtering, keyframe identification via localized UI change, shortcut-free observation frame selection, presence-aware grounding, and two-stage action-space normalization. These refined trajectories are then converted into multi-task training views spanning navigation, planning, forward dynamics, and grounding. We fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B on a subset of the more than one million human-annotation-free training samples generated by this pipeline. Evaluations show that the model achieves consistent gains across multiple benchmarks covering desktop, web, and mobile environments, including OSWorld-G, ScreenSpot-Pro, AndroidControl, and AgentNetBench, indicating improved core capabilities in grounding, step-level instruction execution, and trajectory-level decision-making. Notably, all gains are achieved without any in-distribution training data from target domains. Learning exclusively from trajectories extracted from public videos via the T2T pipeline, the model exhibits cross-application and cross-task generalization capabilities.

title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI

payload.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
payload.abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), for those refined capabilities. Our approach offers several benefits. Firstly, it may demonstrate whether the behaviors of AI systems are aligned, or in a broad sense desirable. Secondly, the debate may inform policy questions (e.g., what models should be deployed in which contexts?). Thirdly, our approach may complement engineering and design efforts: when capabilities can be precisely characterized, they can inform the development of models. Fourthly, applying our moral reasoning concepts in the new context of AI systems should improve our understanding of those concepts.

title: Technical Challenges for Ultra Fine Pitch Hybrid Bonding

payload.title: Technical Challenges for Ultra Fine Pitch Hybrid Bonding
payload.abstract: Hybrid bonding is rapidly emerging as a foundational technology for next-generation advanced packaging, enabling ultra-high-density interconnects required for heterogeneous integration of chiplets, logic, memory, and specialized accelerators. As the industry pushes toward ultra-fine pitch interconnects approaching single- digit microns and below, significant technical challenges must be addressed across the process flow. These challenges include achieving extremely tight wafer and die alignment tolerances, maintaining surface planarity and cleanliness at the nanometer scale, controlling copper dishing and dielectric erosion during CMP, and ensuring defect-free oxide and copper-copper bonding interfaces. In addition, scaling hybrid bonding to ultra-fine pitch requires improvements in metrology, defect inspection, thermal management, and yield control to support high-volume manufacturing. Integration with complementary technologies such as silicon interposers, wafer-to-wafer and die-to-wafer bonding architectures, and heterogeneous material stacks further increases process complexity. This presentation reviews the key technical barriers to ultra-fine pitch hybrid bonding and discusses emerging process solutions and equipment innovations required to enable reliable, high-density interconnects for future high-performance computing, AI, and advanced system-in- package applications.

title: TopSDF: Topological Signed Distance Field for High-Quality Triangle Mesh Extraction from 3D Gaussian Splatting

payload.title: TopSDF: Topological Signed Distance Field for High-Quality Triangle Mesh Extraction from 3D Gaussian Splatting
payload.abstract: Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have demonstrated its effectiveness for photorealistic novel view synthesis. However, extracting clean, watertight, explicit surface meshes from 3DGS remains a critical challenge. Previous methods approximate geometry via discrete Marching Tetrahedra, where each grid vertex is assigned a single scalar signed distance value. At complex geometric boundaries and thin structures, this suboptimal parameterization forces severe compromises across shared vertices, causing gradient collisions and geometric frustration. Furthermore, existing optimization objectives neglect element shape conditioning, producing degenerate triangles. We introduce TopSDF, a framework that models the signed distance state as a multivariate Gaussian random field. By learning latent topological covariances across tetrahedral vertices, our formulation expands local degrees of freedom for SDF estimates, allowing the candidate mesh vertices to be placed flexibly along the bipolar edges in the tetrahedra as driven by such topological correlation. Concurrently, we directly integrate variational meshing energies into the joint optimization, coupled with an energy-driven Gaussian densification strategy to improve triangle mesh quality. Our experiments across Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and ScanNet++ show that TopSDF achieves state-of-the-art mesh-based novel view rendering (+0.86 dB PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360) and triangle-mesh quality (from 0.37 to 0.49 aspect ratio).

title: Different Timescales, Different Signals: Multimodal Landmark-Visibility Prediction in a Long-Term Webcam Network

payload.title: Different Timescales, Different Signals: Multimodal Landmark-Visibility Prediction in a Long-Term Webcam Network
payload.abstract: Scenic visibility is not a single forecasting problem: planning a trip months ahead, deciding whether to go outside today, and judging whether tomorrow will be clear rely on different information. Using a year-scale multimodal archive of Mount Fuji webcams and meteorological observations, we identify a clear hierarchy across timescales. Seasonal climatology provides useful long-range guidance, webcam imagery is the strongest same-day observation (AUC 0.95), and the numerical forecast valid on the target day carries most of the day-specific signal one to three days ahead. Revealing this hierarchy requires evaluation that respects the dependence among cameras observing the same regional weather state: permissive splits substantially overstate multi-day performance, while date-grouped and forward-in-time evaluation reduce the apparent contribution of the current scene and current weather. On 6,575 camera-days, the current visual summary provides no measurable one-day gain once the target-day forecast is available. The remaining opportunity lies at shorter horizons, where the present visual representation discards cloud geometry and motion. These results recast scenic visibility prediction as a multi-timescale sensing problem rather than a single multimodal forecasting task.

title: Small Data in Long-Term Environmental Vision: Annotation Noise, Gamification, and Label-Budget Scaling

payload.title: Small Data in Long-Term Environmental Vision: Annotation Noise, Gamification, and Label-Budget Scaling
payload.abstract: Long-running environmental camera networks produce abundant images but few reliable annotations. Using FujiView, a network of webcams around Mount Fuji, we study three linked questions: whether gamification affects annotation participation and agreement, how annotators disagree on ordinal visibility labels, and how label budget affects downstream classification. Across seven nonrandomized sessions with 22 labelers, gamification showed a more promising pattern for sustained participation than for labeling speed or agreement. In the closest remote-session comparison, the session recorded as gamified had longer active labeling time, while throughput and reference agreement remained similar. Annotation disagreement was substantial at fine granularity: crowd votes matched the single-annotator reference on 49.1% of exact visibility classes, versus 90.2% after grouping them into Good/Poor. In five-replicate label-budget experiments, models using 25% of the available label pool achieved held-out exact accuracy only 2.8 percentage points below the full-pool model on average. Together, these findings highlight the importance of designing reliable annotation targets, evaluating engagement mechanisms without assuming causal benefits, and using empirical scaling curves to plan labeling effort.

title: Swarm Shepherd: Securing Multi-Agent Ecosystems Against Persistent Latent Compromise

payload.title: Swarm Shepherd: Securing Multi-Agent Ecosystems Against Persistent Latent Compromise
payload.abstract: Agentic ecosystems are emerging as a new platform layer in which agents maintain persistent memory, retrieve from shared knowledge bases, execute through tool interfaces, and coordinate through shared states. These capabilities create a security problem that per-turn defenses miss: compromise can accumulate across sessions, agents, and system layers before visible failure. We define this threat as Agentic Sleeper, a system-level adversary that first behaves legitimately, gains routing trust, and later activates across memory, agent logic, and infrastructure. We formulate defense as inference under partial observability and propose Swarm Shepherd, a system-level defense framework centered on an inference filter for early warning, paired with a backward trace-back module for entry attribution. Our analysis yields a two-scale deployment rule that balances longer event histories against broader agent coverage. Across LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen, Agentic Sleeper drift begins 2.7--8.9$\times$ faster than natural baselines, propagates across agents on most topologies, and evades per-turn and stateful defenses above 80\%. Swarm Shepherd warns at least three sessions before visible degradation (2.6 sessions when failure is scored by the benchmark's own task grader), while trace-back reaches 0.69 top-1 accuracy and 0.72 macro-F1 over 24 variants. The two-scale deployment rule is empirically confirmed, and in live end-to-end runs on LangGraph and AutoGen the posterior-guided defense stack drives cross-agent propagation below the self-sustaining regime, which removing only the visibly compromised agent does not achieve.

title: Selection-Aware Certification of Client-Constrained Fraud Rule Portfolios Under Synthetic Distribution Shift

payload.title: Selection-Aware Certification of Client-Constrained Fraud Rule Portfolios Under Synthetic Distribution Shift
payload.abstract: Selecting fraud-rule portfolios to satisfy a precision or recall floor can overfit the data used for selection. We study finite-family certification for bounded OR portfolios, comparing point-estimate selection, a fixed safety margin, and one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bounds with Bonferroni adjustment. In a factorial follow-up with 6,400 datasets from two author-designed synthetic generators, full-validation certification reduced the held-out floor-violation rate by 29.1 percentage points on average versus full-validation point selection, while reducing deployment by 31.7 points. Compared with a fixed 0.05 margin, certification reduced violations by 22.2 points and deployment by 29.4 points; results varied across conditions. Using the full rather than half validation sample increased deployment by 17.1 points on average, without a uniform reduction in shifted-test violations. In a separate 400-dataset no-shift sweep, certification deployment rose from 61.3% to 90.2% as validation size increased from 1,500 to 15,000; no violations occurred among 2,887 deployed portfolios tested on 100,000-row holdouts. A temporal case study on the public synthetic Bank Account Fraud Base dataset used recall at a 5% false-positive-rate cap; the selected candidate pool captured less than 1% of test fraud, showing limited coverage in this setup. Together, these experiments characterize how finite-family certification changes the reliability-deployment tradeoff for bounded OR portfolios under specified synthetic conditions. The evidence covers the evaluated generators and one public synthetic BAF case study; it does not estimate performance on real transaction populations or robustness to arbitrary distribution shift. The authors revised and rewrote this abstract after receiving a draft from OpenAI Codex.

title: PolarGait: Constructing Complementary Views from a Single Human Sketch for Gait Recognition

payload.title: PolarGait: Constructing Complementary Views from a Single Human Sketch for Gait Recognition
payload.abstract: Existing multimodal gait recognition methods exploit complementary information by fusing heterogeneous representations. Whether useful complementarity can be constructed from a single representation before fusion remains less explored. We propose PolarGait, which constructs complementary views of Human Sketch through filtering and spatial reparameterization. Filter-Oriented Sketch Decomposition (FOSD) uses Gaussian smoothing to extract coherent structures and absolute residuals to capture local response differences. Gait-Oriented Polar Transformation (GOPT) combines silhouette-guided sketch normalization, a gait-oriented center, and lower-body-biased non-uniform angular sampling to construct a polar view complementary to the Cartesian representation. Silhouette provides auxiliary global body-shape information. Experiments on CCPG, SUSTech1K, CASIA-B, and Gait3D validate the framework. Under the single-Sketch setting, FOSD+GOPT improves the original Sketch baseline by 6.6% on CCPG and 4.6% on CASIA-B. The complete PolarGait achieves Rank-1 accuracies of 87.9%, 95.2%, 96.6%, and 86.4% on the four benchmarks, respectively. These results show that complementary gait information can be constructed within a single structured representation and integrated for robust gait recognition.

title: Shared Mobile AR Without Depth Sensors from Monocular Point Maps

payload.title: Shared Mobile AR Without Depth Sensors from Monocular Point Maps
payload.abstract: Depth-aware augmented reality on phones needs dense geometry of the surrounding room. iPhones and iPads without LiDAR expose only sparse feature points and detected planes, and ARKit often takes tens of seconds to report the first wall. We describe a scan-free pipeline for these devices. A point-map network (MoGe-2) predicts metric geometry from each camera frame, the remaining depth shift is recovered from the camera intrinsics, and each frame's scale is aligned to views already in the map. A persistent voxel map with visibility-based expiry answers occlusion and collision queries. Co-located devices share one coordinate frame by solving yaw and floor-plane translation from sightings of each other. We evaluate the deployed system on 309 device-sessions from 19 device models without LiDAR, with 179 device-sessions from LiDAR phones in the same deployment as a reference population. A first dense depth map was recorded within 10 s in 80% of sessions, while ARKit had reported a wall plane by then in 25%. The median session scale was 0.98 against ARKit's wall planes and 1.00 against its camera translation. Scale changed by a median of 9% between nearby frames, against 0.4% with LiDAR, and depth points spread three times as widely around walls. In multi-device sessions, 69% of devices without LiDAR reached a converged shared frame, against 84% of LiDAR phones. The main remaining error is scale that changes from frame to frame.

title: SynPanZ: A Synthetic Dataset to Improve Multi-Animal Pose Estimation in Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes)

payload.title: SynPanZ: A Synthetic Dataset to Improve Multi-Animal Pose Estimation in Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes)
payload.abstract: Pose estimation underpins a wide range of automated monitoring workflows in animal behaviour research. Unfortunately, endangered great apes such as chimpanzees suffer a chronic shortage of the type of hand-annotated training data that has made robust pose estimation in humans and other model organisms possible. This paper introduces SynPanZ, a synthetically generated dataset for pose estimation in great apes. Our pipeline renders multi-individual scenes from rigged, behaviourally animated chimpanzee models with randomised poses, lighting conditions, environmental contexts, and camera motion, producing animated RGB videos with per-instance 2D keypoint locations without manual labelling. To test whether synthetic augmentation improves cross-dataset generalisation, four DeepLabCut models are trained under matched settings on data sourced from DeepWild with varying real-to-synthetic augmentation ratios. Models are evaluated on ChimpACT, a visually disjoint zoo dataset. We find that augmenting the DeepWild training data with approximately three times as many synthetic frames nearly doubles instance coverage (12.34% to 22.54%) while maintaining keypoint localisation accuracy on detected individuals (PCK@0.20: 49.71% to 52.25%). Synthetic-only training fails, showing that rendered data complements rather than replaces real annotated data. This work represents a step towards reliable pose estimation for great apes.

title: Exists, Valid: Calibrated Validity of Stored 3D Geometry Across Long Observation Gaps

payload.title: Exists, Valid: Calibrated Validity of Stored 3D Geometry Across Long Observation Gaps
payload.abstract: Repeated airborne LiDAR surveys are costly, while stored 3D geometry can become outdated between observations. Existing change-detection methods compare observed epochs. However, they do not quantify the validity of geometry that has not been revisited. We distinguish observation, existence and geometric validity using a probabilistic filter over five geometric transitions: persistence, modification, growth, removal and replacement. The framework learns class-specific continuous-time transition priors from interval-censored observations and combines shape residuals with LiDAR free-space evidence. Functional anchors enable prior sharing across sites with different survey frequencies. In controlled experiments with misspecified dynamics and 60% visibility, our method reduces combined error from 36.9% to 16.5% and expected calibration error (ECE) from 0.19-0.32 to 0.017. Cross-site sharing reduces ECE at two-survey sites from 0.156 to 0.029. On Urb3DCD-v2, the method achieves 9.8% combined error and 0.016 ECE, outperforming baselines at 12.6% and at least 0.070, respectively. Re-survey prioritisation improves only modestly over random selection with two observations. Code and an evaluation protocol are released at https://github.com/anwaarua/life4d.

title: ReMoVe: Refining a Video Model's Own Motion for Coherent Human Video Generation

payload.title: ReMoVe: Refining a Video Model's Own Motion for Coherent Human Video Generation
payload.abstract: Video generation models have become increasingly capable of synthesizing realistic human motion, yet they often lose track of the very structure that makes the motion plausible. As generated human motion becomes more complex, videos can suffer from progressive body deformation and appearance drift across frames. Existing motion-controlled methods use explicit representations to stabilize generation, but typically rely on pre-defined motion sequences as references. This raises a fundamental question: if the base generator already produces a usable coarse motion, why replace it with an external one? ReMoVe answers this question by treating the coarse output as a motion hypothesis rather than a final result. ReMoVe recovers and refines the underlying motion, then renders the refined motion as 3D mesh and transfers facial appearance onto it, thereby improving motion accuracy and identity consistency. We further derive depth from the same 3D scene and camera trajectory to impose scene-level spatial consistency beyond the mesh. By jointly conditioning video generation models on mesh and depth, ReMoVe synthesizes high-quality motion videos with controllable camera trajectories and enhanced spatio-temporal consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReMoVe improves human structural stability, appearance consistency, temporal coherence, and motion-following fidelity, while retaining the base generator's motion prior and offering accurate camera control.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical decision support: device regulation and decision influence.

payload.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical decision support: device regulation and decision influence.
payload.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled clinical decision support (CDS) challenges core assumptions of the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) recently updated CDS guidance, including the concepts of independent clinician review of outputs and manufacturer-intended use for exempting certain CDS tools from medical device regulation. We examine the FDA's January 2026 CDS guidance in the context of the evolving landscape of AI-enabled CDS tools, clinician interaction studies with AI-enabled CDS, and AI governance frameworks. Although the FDA's framework distinguishes non-device CDS from regulated software, AI-enabled CDS may synthesize and transform clinical information in ways that are difficult to verify during routine care, increasing clinician susceptibility to automation bias. Incorporating pragmatic triggers into existing governance frameworks can help identify scenarios with a heightened risk for clinical decision influence. Oversight calibrated to real-world clinical decision influence is needed to strengthen practical safety standards for AI-enabled CDS.

title: From Sparse to Dense: Camera Relocalization with Scene-Specific Detector from Feature Gaussian Splatting

payload.title: From Sparse to Dense: Camera Relocalization with Scene-Specific Detector from Feature Gaussian Splatting
payload.abstract: This paper presents a novel camera relocalization method, STDLoc, which leverages Feature Gaussian as scene representation. STDLoc is a full relocalization pipeline that can achieve accurate relocalization without relying on any pose prior. Unlike previous coarse-to-fine localization methods that require image retrieval first and then feature matching, we propose a novel sparse-to-dense localization paradigm. Based on this scene representation, we introduce a novel matching-oriented Gaussian sampling strategy and a scene-specific detector to achieve efficient and robust initial pose estimation. Furthermore, based on the initial localization results, we align the query feature map to the Gaussian feature field by dense feature matching to enable accurate localization. The experiments on indoor and outdoor datasets show that STDLoc outperforms current state-of-the-art localization methods in terms of localization accuracy and recall. Our code is available on the project website: https://zju3dv.github.io/STDLoc.

title: HQC-NBV: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical View Planning Approach

payload.title: HQC-NBV: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical View Planning Approach
payload.abstract: Efficient view planning is a fundamental challenge in computer vision and robotic perception, critical for tasks ranging from search and rescue operations to autonomous navigation. While classical approaches, including sampling-based and deterministic methods, have shown promise in planning camera viewpoints for scene exploration, they often struggle with computational scalability and solution optimality in complex settings. This study introduces HQC-NBV, a hybrid quantum-classical framework for view planning that leverages quantum properties to efficiently explore the parameter space while maintaining robustness and scalability. We propose a specific Hamiltonian formulation with multi-component cost terms and a parameter-centric variational ansatz with bidirectional alternating entanglement patterns that capture the hierarchical dependencies between viewpoint parameters. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that quantum-specific components provide measurable performance advantages. Compared to the classical methods, our approach achieves up to 49.2% higher exploration efficiency across diverse environments. Our analysis of entanglement architecture and coherence-preserving terms provides insights into the mechanisms of quantum advantage in robotic exploration tasks. This work represents a significant advancement in integrating quantum computing into robotic perception systems, offering a paradigm-shifting solution for various robot vision tasks.

title: DynPose: Largely Improving the Efficiency of Human Pose Estimation by a Simple Dynamic Framework

payload.title: DynPose: Largely Improving the Efficiency of Human Pose Estimation by a Simple Dynamic Framework
payload.abstract: Top-down approaches for human pose estimation (HPE) have reached a high level of sophistication, exemplified by models such as HRNet and ViTPose. Nonetheless, the low efficiency of top-down methods is a recognized issue that has not been sufficiently explored in current research. Our analysis suggests that the primary cause of inefficiency stems from the substantial diversity found in pose samples. On one hand, simple poses can be accurately estimated without requiring the computational resources of larger models. On the other hand, a more prominent issue arises from the abundance of bounding boxes, which remain excessive even after NMS. In this paper, we present a straightforward yet effective dynamic framework called DynPose, designed to match diverse pose samples with the most appropriate models, thereby ensuring optimal performance and high efficiency. Specifically, the framework contains a lightweight router and two pre-trained HPE models: one small and one large. The router is optimized to classify samples and dynamically determine the appropriate inference paths. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework. For example, using ResNet-50 and HRNet-W32 as the pretrained models, our DynPose achieves an almost 50% increase in speed over HRNet-W32 while maintaining the same-level accuracy. More importantly, the framework can be generalized to other pre-trained models and datasets without re-training or fine-tuning. Code is available at https://github.com/Aritoria/DynPose.

title: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation

payload.title: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation
payload.abstract: The rapid development of large vision-language model (VLM) has greatly promoted the research of GUI agent. However, GUI agents still face significant challenges in handling long-horizon tasks. First, single-agent models struggle to balance high-level capabilities and low-level execution capability, facing prevalent issues of responsibility coupling and capability conflicts. Second, agents lack awareness of the task state, leading to progress loss in long-horizon tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a staged execution-feedback reinforcement learning algorithm. Unlike training a unified policy model, we focus on training high-level scheduling models. Specifically, we propose and train two agents: a Coordinator, responsible for the strategic planning and task decomposition; and a State Tracker, responsible for context compression and information management to maintain the task's state and coherence. Based on this, we built the Coordinator-Executor-State Tracker (CES) multi-agent framework, which can be integrated with any low-level Executor model, assisting the Executor in solving long-horizon tasks through task scheduling and state management. Experiments on long-horizon task benchmarks demonstrate that CES significantly enhances the system's planning and state management capabilities. Furthermore, analysis confirms that our trained high-level scheduling module is a generalizable, plug-and-play module that significantly enhances the long-horizon capabilities of various Executors. Code can be available at https://github.com/hehehahi4/CES.

title: UnReflectAnything: RGB-Only Highlight Removal by Rendering Synthetic Specular Supervision

payload.title: UnReflectAnything: RGB-Only Highlight Removal by Rendering Synthetic Specular Supervision
payload.abstract: Specular highlights distort appearance, obscure texture, and hinder geometric reasoning in both natural and surgical imagery. We present UnReflectAnything, an RGB-only framework that removes highlights from a single image by predicting a highlight map together with a reflection-free diffuse reconstruction. The model uses a frozen vision transformer encoder to extract multi-scale features, a lightweight head to localize specular regions, and a token-level inpainting module that restores corrupted feature patches before producing the final diffuse image. To overcome the lack of paired supervision, we introduce a Virtual Highlight Synthesis pipeline that renders physically plausible specularities using monocular geometry, Fresnel-aware shading, and randomized lighting which enables training on arbitrary RGB images with correct geometric structure. UnReflectAnything generalizes across natural and surgical domains where non-Lambertian surfaces and non-uniform lighting create severe highlights and it achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks. Project Page: https://alberto-rota.github.io/UnReflectAnything/

title: SoccerMaster: A Vision Foundation Model for Soccer Understanding

payload.title: SoccerMaster: A Vision Foundation Model for Soccer Understanding
payload.abstract: Soccer understanding has recently garnered growing research interest due to its domain-specific complexity and unique challenges. Unlike prior works that typically rely on isolated, task-specific expert models, this work aims to propose a unified model to handle diverse soccer visual understanding tasks, ranging from fine-grained perception (e.g., athlete detection and identification) to high-level semantic reasoning (e.g., event classification). Concretely, our contributions are threefold: (i) we present SoccerMaster, the first soccer-specific vision foundation model that unifies diverse tasks within a single framework via supervised multi-task pretraining; (ii) we develop an automated data curation pipeline, SoccerFactory, to generate scalable spatial annotations, and integrate multiple existing soccer video datasets as a comprehensive pretraining data resource for multi-task pretraining; and (iii) we conduct extensive evaluations demonstrating that SoccerMaster consistently outperforms task-specific expert models across diverse downstream tasks, highlighting its breadth and superiority. The data, code, and model will be publicly available.

title: Empowering Vector Graphics with Consistently Arbitrary Viewing and View-dependent Visibility

payload.title: Empowering Vector Graphics with Consistently Arbitrary Viewing and View-dependent Visibility
payload.abstract: This work presents a novel text-to-vector graphics generation approach, Dream3DVG, allowing for arbitrary viewpoint viewing, progressive detail optimization, and view-dependent occlusion awareness. Our approach is a dual-branch optimization framework, consisting of an auxiliary 3D Gaussian Splatting optimization branch and a 3D vector graphics optimization branch. The introduced 3DGS branch can bridge the domain gaps between text prompts and vector graphics with more consistent guidance. Moreover, 3DGS allows for progressive detail control by scheduling classifier-free guidance, facilitating guiding vector graphics with coarse shapes at the initial stages and finer details at later stages. We also improve the view-dependent occlusions by devising a visibility-awareness rendering module. Extensive results on 3D sketches and 3D iconographies, demonstrate the superiority of the method on different abstraction levels of details, cross-view consistency, and occlusion-aware stroke culling. Code is available at https://github.com/chenxinl/Dream3DVG.git.

title: UniGoal: Towards Universal Zero-shot Goal-oriented Navigation

payload.title: UniGoal: Towards Universal Zero-shot Goal-oriented Navigation
payload.abstract: In this paper, we propose a general framework for universal zero-shot goal-oriented navigation. Existing zero-shot methods build inference framework upon large language models (LLM) for specific tasks, which differs a lot in overall pipeline and fails to generalize across different types of goal. Towards the aim of universal zero-shot navigation, we propose a uniform graph representation to unify different goals, including object category, instance image and text description. We also convert the observation of agent into an online maintained scene graph. With this consistent scene and goal representation, we preserve most structural information compared with pure text and are able to leverage LLM for explicit graph-based reasoning. Specifically, we conduct graph matching between the scene graph and goal graph at each time instant and propose different strategies to generate long-term goal of exploration according to different matching states. The agent first iteratively searches subgraph of goal when zero-matched. With partial matching, the agent then utilizes coordinate projection and anchor pair alignment to infer the goal location. Finally scene graph correction and goal verification are applied for perfect matching. We also present a blacklist mechanism to enable robust switch between stages. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks show that our UniGoal achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on three studied navigation tasks with a single model, even outperforming task-specific zero-shot methods and supervised universal methods. Project Page.

title: NeAR: Coupled Neural Asset-Renderer Stack

payload.title: NeAR: Coupled Neural Asset-Renderer Stack
payload.abstract: Neural asset authoring and neural rendering have traditionally evolved as disjoint paradigms: one generates digital assets for fixed graphics pipelines, while the other maps conventional assets to images. However, treating them as independent entities limits the potential for end-to-end optimization in fidelity and consistency. In this paper, we bridge this gap with NeAR, a Coupled Neural Asset--Renderer Stack. We argue that co-designing the asset representation and the renderer creates a robust"contract"for superior generation. On the asset side, we introduce the Lighting-Homogenized SLAT (LH-SLAT). Leveraging a rectified-flow model, NeAR lifts casually lit single images into a canonical, illumination-invariant latent space, effectively suppressing baked-in shadows and highlights. On the renderer side, we design a lighting-aware neural decoder tailored to interpret these homogenized latents. Conditioned on HDR environment maps and camera views, it synthesizes relightable 3D Gaussian splats in real-time without per-object optimization. We validate NeAR on four tasks: (1) G-buffer-based forward rendering, (2) random-lit reconstruction, (3) unknown-lit relighting, and (4) novel-view relighting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our coupled stack outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both quantitative metrics and perceptual quality. We hope this coupled asset-renderer perspective inspires future graphics stacks that view neural assets and renderers as co-designed components instead of independent entities.

title: RDD: Robust Feature Detector and Descriptor using Deformable Transformer

payload.title: RDD: Robust Feature Detector and Descriptor using Deformable Transformer
payload.abstract: As a core step in structure-from-motion and SLAM, robust feature detection and description under challenging scenarios such as significant viewpoint changes remain unresolved despite their ubiquity. While recent works have identified the importance of local features in modeling geometric transformations, these methods fail to learn the visual cues present in long-range relationships. We present Robust Deformable Detector (RDD), a novel and robust keypoint detector/descriptor leveraging the deformable transformer, which captures global context and geometric invariance through deformable self-attention mechanisms. Specifically, we observed that deformable attention focuses on key locations, effectively reducing the search space complexity and modeling the geometric invariance. Furthermore, we collected an Air-to-Ground dataset for training in addition to the standard MegaDepth dataset. Our proposed method outperforms all state-of-the-art keypoint detection/description methods in sparse matching tasks and is also capable of semi-dense matching. To ensure comprehensive evaluation, we introduce two challenging benchmarks: one emphasizing large viewpoint and scale variations, and the other being an Air-to-Ground benchmark — an evaluation setting that has recently gaining popularity for 3D reconstruction across different altitudes. Project page: https://xtcpete.github.io/rdd/.

title: RICCARDO: Radar Hit Prediction and Convolution for Camera-Radar 3D Object Detection

payload.title: RICCARDO: Radar Hit Prediction and Convolution for Camera-Radar 3D Object Detection
payload.abstract: Radar hits reflect from points on both the boundary and internal to object outlines. This results in a complex distribution of radar hits that depends on factors including object category, size and orientation. Current radar-camera fusion methods implicitly account for this with a black-box neural network. In this paper, we explicitly utilize a radar hit distribution model to assist fusion. First, we build a model to predict radar hit distributions conditioned on object properties obtained from a monocular detector. Second, we use the predicted distribution as a kernel to match actual measured radar points in the neighborhood of the monocular detections, generating matching scores at nearby positions. Finally, a fusion stage combines context with the kernel detector to refine the matching scores. Our method achieves the state-of-the-art radar-camera detection performance on nuScenes. Our source code is available at https://github.com/longyunf/riccardo.

title: Generating 6DoF Object Manipulation Trajectories from Action Description in Egocentric Vision

payload.title: Generating 6DoF Object Manipulation Trajectories from Action Description in Egocentric Vision
payload.abstract: Learning to use tools or objects in common scenes, particularly handling them in various ways as instructed, is a key challenge for developing interactive robots. Training models to generate such manipulation trajectories requires a large and diverse collection of detailed manipulation demonstrations for various objects, which is nearly unfeasible to gather at scale. In this paper, we propose a framework that leverages large-scale ego- and exo-centric video datasets — constructed globally with substantial effort — of Exo-Ego4D to extract diverse manipulation trajectories at scale. From these extracted trajectories with the associated textual action description, we develop trajectory generation models based on visual and point cloud-based language models. In the recently proposed egocentric vision-based in-a-quality trajectory dataset of HOT3D, we confirmed that our models successfully generate valid object trajectories, establishing a training dataset and baseline models for the novel task of generating 6DoF manipulation trajectories from action descriptions in egocentric vision. Our dataset and code: https://biscue5.github.io/egoscaler-project-page/.

title: DnLUT: Ultra-Efficient Color Image Denoising via Channel-Aware Lookup Tables

payload.title: DnLUT: Ultra-Efficient Color Image Denoising via Channel-Aware Lookup Tables
payload.abstract: While deep neural networks have revolutionized image de-noising capabilities, their deployment on edge devices remains challenging due to substantial computational and memory requirements. To this end, we present DnLUT, an ultra-efficient lookup table-based framework that achieves high-quality color image denoising with minimal resource consumption. Our key innovation lies in two complementary components: a Pairwise Channel Mixer (PCM) that effectively captures inter-channel correlations and spatial dependencies in parallel, and a novel L-shaped convolution design that maximizes receptive field coverage while minimizing storage overhead. By converting these components into optimized lookup tables post-training, DnLUT achieves remarkable efficiency - requiring only 500KB storage and 0.1% energy consumption compared to its CNN contestant DnCNN, while delivering 20× faster inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DnLUT outperforms all existing LUT-based methods by over 1dB in PSNR, establishing a new state-of-the-art in resource-efficient color image de-noising. The project is available at https://github.com/Stephen0808/DnLUT.

title: Comprehensive Relighting: Generalizable and Consistent Monocular Human Relighting and Harmonization

payload.title: Comprehensive Relighting: Generalizable and Consistent Monocular Human Relighting and Harmonization
payload.abstract: This paper introduces Comprehensive Relighting, the first all-in-one approach that can both control and harmonize the lighting from an image or video of humans with arbitrary body parts from any scene. Building such a generalizable model is extremely challenging due to the lack of dataset, restricting existing image-based relighting models to a specific scenario (e.g., face or static human). To address this challenge, we repurpose a pre-trained diffusion model as a general image prior and jointly model the human relighting and background harmonization in the coarse-to-fine framework. To further enhance the temporal coherence of the relighting, we introduce an unsupervised temporal lighting model that learns the lighting cycle consistency from many real-world videos without any ground truth. In inference time, our temporal lighting module is combined with the diffusion models through the spatio-temporal feature blending algorithms without extra training; and we apply a new guided refinement as a post-processing to pre-serve the high-frequency details from the input image. In the experiments, Comprehensive Relighting shows a strong generalizability and lighting temporal coherence, outperforming existing image-based human relighting and harmonization methods.

title: Reading or Reasoning? Format Decoupled Reinforcement Learning for Document OCR

payload.title: Reading or Reasoning? Format Decoupled Reinforcement Learning for Document OCR
payload.abstract: Reading text from images or scanned documents via OCR models has been a longstanding focus of researchers. Intuitively, text reading is perceived as a straightforward perceptual task, and existing work primarily focuses on constructing enriched data engineering to enhance SFT capabilities. In this work, we observe that even advanced OCR models exhibit significantly higher entropy in formatted text (\emph{e.g.}, formula, table, etc.) compared to plain text, often by an order of magnitude. These statistical patterns reveal that advanced OCR models struggle with high output uncertainty when dealing with format sensitive document, suggesting that reasoning over diverse reading pathways may improve OCR performance. To address this, we propose format decoupled reinforcement learning (FD-RL), which leverages high-entropy patterns for targeted optimization. Our approach employs entropy-based data filtration strategy to identify format-intensive instances, and adopt format decoupled rewards tailored to different format types, enabling format-level validation rather than token-level memorization. FD-RL achieves an average score of 90.41 on OmniDocBench, setting a new record for end-to-end models on this highly popular benchmark. More importantly, we conduct comprehensive ablation studies over data, training, filtering, and rewarding strategies, thoroughly validating their effectiveness.

title: SimScale: Learning to Drive via Real-World Simulation at Scale

payload.title: SimScale: Learning to Drive via Real-World Simulation at Scale
payload.abstract: Achieving fully autonomous driving systems requires learning rational decisions in a wide span of scenarios, including safety-critical and out-of-distribution ones. However, such cases are underrepresented in real-world corpus collected by human experts. To complement for the lack of data diversity, we introduce a novel and scalable simulation framework capable of synthesizing massive unseen states upon existing driving logs. Our pipeline utilizes advanced neural rendering with a reactive environment to generate high-fidelity multi-view observations controlled by the perturbed ego trajectory. Furthermore, we develop a pseudo-expert trajectory generation mechanism for these newly simulated states to provide action supervision. Upon the synthesized data, we find that a simple co-training strategy on both real-world and simulated samples can lead to significant improvements in both robustness and generalization for various planning methods on challenging real-world benchmarks, up to +8.6 EPDMS on navhard and +2.9 on navtest. More importantly, such policy improvement scales smoothly by increasing simulation data only, even without extra real-world data streaming in. We further reveal several crucial findings of such a sim-real learning system, which we term SimScale, including the design of pseudo-experts and the scaling properties for different policy architectures. Simulation data and code have been released at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/SimScale.

title: Hearing Anywhere in Any Environment

payload.title: Hearing Anywhere in Any Environment
payload.abstract: In mixed reality applications, a realistic acoustic experience in spatial environments is as crucial as the visual experience for achieving true immersion. Despite recent advances in neural approaches for Room Impulse Response (RIR) estimation, most existing methods are limited to the single environment on which they are trained, lacking the ability to generalize to new rooms with different geometries and surface materials. We aim to develop a unified model capable of reconstructing the spatial acoustic experience of any environment with minimum additional measurements. To this end, we present xRIR, a framework for cross-room RIR prediction. The core of our generalizable approach lies in combining a geometric feature extractor, which captures spatial context from panorama depth images, with a RIR encoder that extracts detailed acoustic features from only a few reference RIR samples. To evaluate our method, we introduce AcousticRooms, a new dataset featuring high-fidelity simulation of over 300,000 RIRs from 260 rooms. Experiments show that our method strongly outperforms a series of baselines. Furthermore, we successfully perform sim-to-real transfer by evaluating our model on four real-world environments, demonstrating the generalizability of our approach and the realism of our dataset.

title: FRAME: Floor-aligned Representation for Avatar Motion from Egocentric Video

payload.title: FRAME: Floor-aligned Representation for Avatar Motion from Egocentric Video
payload.abstract: Egocentric motion capture with a head-mounted body-facing stereo camera is crucial for VR and AR applications but presents significant challenges such as heavy occlusions and limited annotated real-world data. Existing methods rely on synthetic pretraining and struggle to generate smooth and accurate predictions in real-world settings, particularly for lower limbs. Our work addresses these limitations by introducing a lightweight VR-based data collection setup with on-board, real-time 6D pose tracking. Using this setup, we collected the most extensive real-world dataset for ego-facing ego-mounted cameras to date in size and motion variability. Effectively integrating this multimodal input –device pose and camera feeds –is challenging due to the differing characteristics of each data source. To address this, we propose FRAME, a simple yet effective architecture that combines device pose and camera feeds for state-of-the-art body pose prediction through geometrically sound multimodal integration and can run at 300 FPS on modern hardware. Lastly, we showcase a novel training strategy to enhance the model’s generalization capabilities. Our approach exploits the problem’s geometric properties, yielding high-quality motion capture free from common artifacts in prior work. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations, along with extensive comparisons, demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.
