Differences between models are concentrated in question answering, while entity extraction quality limits what entity-level metrics can reveal.

title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development

payload.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
payload.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a well-established paradigm for augmenting large language models (LLMs) with information retrieved from external corpora. However, developing effective RAG systems requires substantial engineering effort and iterative experimentation, as effective design choices vary across tasks and domains. With rapid advances in LLM agent capabilities, we ask how well these agents can autonomously build RAG systems and how effectively they can improve them through iteration. In this paper, we propose AutoRAGBench, the first benchmark to evaluate how well LLM agents develop RAG systems from scratch in an open code space. It comprises nine RAG system development tasks. For each task, agents build RAG systems from scratch without starter code or prescribed strategies, under a six-hour budget on a single H800 GPU. They analyze task data, implement RAG pipelines, and iteratively refine their designs based on experimental feedback. We evaluate nine agent configurations and analyze both the effectiveness of the resulting RAG systems and their development trajectories. GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex CLI achieves the highest average score of 56.1. The composite Human-SOTA baseline averages 44.4. These results show that LLM agents can automate effective RAG system development. When starting from a human-designed system on each of seven tasks, GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex CLI improves the score by 16.6 points on average.

title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash

payload.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
payload.abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scaling experience banks, introducing substantial storage and search overhead that challenges the capacity, bandwidth, and power constraints of edge systems. We propose FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents. FlashX exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage. Proprioception-aware clustering further reduces search overhead and enables incremental experience acquisition without global reclustering. Evaluations across VLA and WAM workloads demonstrate up to 12.24\%p and 7.43\%p improvements in task success under dense and compute-efficient configurations, respectively. FlashX achieves 2.57$\times$ higher search throughput than the strongest prior NAND search architecture under pSLC sensing, with a further 9.7$\times$ search reduction through clustering. This delivers 1.29--3.95$\times$ end-to-end speedup and 1.12--2.34$\times$ energy efficiency improvement over SSD-based retrieval.

title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification

payload.title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
payload.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical learning architectures provide a promising framework for integrating quantum feature transformations into complex data-processing tasks. Among these transformations, the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) offers a structured approach to feature processing, motivating an investigation of how its circuit configuration influences predictive performance, quantum resource requirements, and noise robustness. We present a hybrid PointNet-quantum neural network architecture for LiDAR point-cloud classification, combining classical feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit. Five Fourier-processing configurations are systematically evaluated: No-QFT, Full-QFT-After, QFT-no-swap, IQFT-After, and Trainable-QFT. Experiments on KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet across three random seeds assess classification performance, class-level behavior, circuit complexity, and sensitivity to the IBM FakeManilaV2 noise model. Under ideal simulation, IQFT-After achieves the highest weighted F1-score on KITTI (0.857 $\pm$ 0.033), compared with 0.838 $\pm$ 0.023 for No-QFT. Removing the final SWAP gates in the QFT circuit reduces circuit complexity while preserving the Pauli-Z measurement features up to a fixed permutation that can be absorbed by the classification head. Under quantum noise, the circuit ranking changes, with IQFT-After exhibiting greater performance degradation and No-QFT and Trainable-QFT showing stronger robustness. Per-class analysis further identifies dataset-dependent differences in minority-class performance. These results demonstrate that Fourier-processing configuration influences both classification behavior and noise sensitivity, highlighting the role of circuit structure and hardware-aware evaluation in hybrid quantum learning for three-dimensional point-cloud data.

title: Trajectory-Calibrated Merging of Embodied Policies

payload.title: Trajectory-Calibrated Merging of Embodied Policies
payload.abstract: Robot foundation models are increasingly adapted into task specialists to expand their embodied capabilities. Yet these capabilities remain fragmented across separate policies, and existing model-merging methods do not reliably preserve them during closed-loop execution: parameter-space alignment provides only an indirect proxy for behavior, while regression may fail to preserve behavior at states not covered by its calibration inputs. We present Trajectory-Calibrated Regression (TCR), an execution-aware, gradient-free framework that consolidates robot specialists into a single policy. Across two complementary timescales, TCR collects calibration inputs from expert rollouts spanning different stages of task execution and from intermediate states within iterative action generation. To account for representation shifts introduced by merging, TCR recomputes each block's input through the already merged blocks. It then uses each expert's computation within the block to form module inputs and fits merged weights to match the experts' linear outputs. A two-pass calibration procedure further refines the merged policy using separate rollout caches while retaining the frozen specialists as teachers. The resulting model preserves the original inference graph and requires neither expert routing nor additional gradient training. On LIBERO, TCR merges four $π_{0.5}$ specialists and achieves 77.83% success across 1,200 evaluation episodes, outperforming FeatCal, RegMean, and direct weight averaging by 9.50, 24.17, and 33.00 percentage points, respectively.

title: Reinforcement-Aligned Probabilistic Weather Forecasting with Discrete Tokens

payload.title: Reinforcement-Aligned Probabilistic Weather Forecasting with Discrete Tokens
payload.abstract: Global medium-range weather forecasting must not only generate ensembles efficiently to characterize uncertainty in future states, but also serve downstream applications such as extreme-event warnings and cross-sphere coupled simulations. We introduce WeatherCraft, a framework that unifies probabilistic generation and reinforcement learning alignment through discrete weather tokens, bringing the GPT-style pretraining--post-training paradigm to global medium-range weather forecasting. A multiscale tokenizer represents atmospheric states as a coarse-to-fine token hierarchy, while a Transformer models causal dependencies across time and scale and predicts tokens within each scale in parallel. Direct sampling generates diverse ensembles, and exact token log-probabilities enable Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to maximize downstream task rewards without differentiating through evaluators or coupled models. On the ERA5 benchmark, WeatherCraft's eight-member ensemble mean reduces day-15 normalized RMSE by 17.6% relative to the strongest evaluated deterministic baseline and, with KV caching, achieves an approximately $18\times$ inference speedup over GenCast. Direct fair-CRPS adaptation improves ensemble probabilistic skill, while reward-based post-training improves forecasts of persistent land temperature extremes and coupled ocean heat extremes. This work establishes discrete autoregressive modeling as a general foundation for scalable, task-alignable Earth system foundation models.

title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing

payload.title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing
payload.abstract: Aerial sensing must combine uncertain overhead context with current observations while budgeting prediction, movement and image processing. AeroBelief uses the next executable action as the unit of verification against reference scores. It groups candidate views by first action, scans them with an inexpensive proposer, and selectively queries a structured world model (WM). Calibrated group bounds support strict commitment; a six-query controller connects selective prediction with belief updates, acceptance checks and scheduled sensing. Across four layout families, 40 worlds and 960 closed-loop executions, the AeroBelief controller completes 75.42% of tasks, compared with 73.33% for exhaustive WM scoring and 65.83% for line-of-sight geometry, using 91.81% fewer reference-candidate evaluations than exhaustive scoring. In fixed-reference replay with a six-query cap, proposer-scaled anchored bounds raised first-action certificate availability from 36.25% to 54.69% and reduced mean queries per state by 13.54% relative to unit-scale anchored bounds. A complete ground-hosted pipeline processes 2,685 self-collected 20-megapixel unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images from seven DJI Mavic 3M routes. Context-guided admission and feedback retain all eight independently supported target confirmations with 76.05% fewer processed images and 70.02% less accumulated active processing service than uncapped all-frame processing; feedback saves another 5.17% of images relative to static context. The studies connect budgeted action selection with evidence-driven processing of recorded flight imagery.

title: Passing NPCR Without Diffusion: Exact Signatures, a Detection Benchmark and an Audit of Published Image Ciphers

payload.title: Passing NPCR Without Diffusion: Exact Signatures, a Detection Benchmark and an Audit of Published Image Ciphers
payload.abstract: NPCR, the share of ciphertext bytes changed by a one-pixel plaintext change, is reported for nearly every image cipher as evidence of diffusion, with 99.61% the target. Several mechanisms produce values near it, and the mean does not say which. We separate three regimes: no propagation, one round of forward and backward chaining linear over addition or XOR, and independent ciphertexts. For the second an exact count applies. After a least-significant-bit change its mean asymptotically matches the independent-ciphertext reference, while its spread without cancellation is about five to twenty times larger. In simulation, the one-sided NPCR test of Wu, Noonan and Agaian flags one-round additive, mixed and S-box chaining in 2-4% of papers; read in both directions, the same five values flag at least 99.9%. Two-sided testing does the detecting; the spread and the other signatures help diagnose the structure. We then audit twenty-one published schemes. The count matches a reimplementation of one published diffusion layer on every trial and accounts for its reported table, the signatures show two schemes whose printed specifications cannot produce their reported values, and find that three of our own report plain-versus-cipher values and fall to two chosen images; ten more change their encryption material with the plaintext or per encryption, so their NPCR mostly reflects that change. A released checker applies the signatures to published tables, showing what a table measures within stated assumptions; it does not certify security.

title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction

payload.title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction
payload.abstract: Task-specific rubrics are increasingly used to evaluate open-ended language-model outputs, yet constructing comprehensive evaluation criteria from complex source documents remains challenging. We study automatic rubric construction in professional mergers and acquisitions (M&A) due diligence, where evaluation criteria must be inferred from task instructions and supporting documents without access to an expert-authored reference rubric. We introduce a multi-axis generation framework that explores complementary structural and free-form views of the source evidence to construct a broad pool of candidate evaluation criteria. To distinguish failures of criterion discovery from failures of candidate selection, we introduce the coverage-selection gap, which measures the difference between reference-free ranking and a reference-informed greedy diagnostic under a fixed selection budget. Developed on 16 tasks and evaluated on four held-out tasks, our framework achieves 0.876 macro recall against senior-authored reference rubrics under an LLM-based criterion-equivalence protocol. Ablation studies further show that introducing new structural search axes improves recall by 6-10 percentage points, whereas increasing generation volume along existing search directions yields at most 1.5 points. These findings suggest that, once a high-coverage candidate pool has been constructed, effective reference-free selection becomes a substantial bottleneck in document-grounded rubric construction.

title: TwoPass: Draft-Guided Few-Step Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation

payload.title: TwoPass: Draft-Guided Few-Step Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation
payload.abstract: Action-conditioned video prediction lets robots anticipate the visual consequences of their actions for planning and policy evaluation. Existing predictors denoise each future from noise without using their own estimate of it, which limits the quality of the predicted future, in particular of the manipulated objects, and requires many network calls. We present TwoPass, a self-conditioned training-and-inference framework that keeps the standard flow-matching objective. Self-Generated Draft Training supplies a detached clean-video estimate from the shared network as conditioning at the same noisy state. A Refinement-Only Late Adapter applies a dedicated residual transformation when a draft is present. At inference, Draft-Reuse Iterative Refinement obtains both a solver update and the next draft from each velocity prediction, requiring as few as 4 function evaluations (NFE) per video chunk. Training samples discrete solver-query noise levels and updates the pretrained backbone. Extensive experiments on Bridge and Language Table show that TwoPass achieves state-of-the-art results with 4 NFE, far fewer than the 50-59 calls of existing predictors. Code: https://github.com/PlantPotatoOnMoon/TwoPass.

title: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds

payload.title: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds
payload.abstract: Multimodal agents can now build interactive 3D worlds and games, yet these worlds, like those built by people, often contain glitches such as floating objects, walls that can be walked through, or objects that change when no one is looking. An automatic auditor could check such worlds at scale and provide rewards for agents that build them, but only if it is both accurate and cheap. Auditing requires three abilities, namely navigating to the objects that may contain a glitch, triggering glitches that appear only after a specific behavior, and recognizing what is wrong. Current auditors are either accurate but slow and expensive or cheap but unreliable. We study how much of the audit small models can take on. A 4B vision language model fine-tuned end to end on verified trajectories of a frontier teacher guided by Bayesian search learns to navigate and trigger, and six such explorers together match a frontier model on both, but recognition stays far behind. We therefore build an auditor in which a swarm of small explorers navigates and triggers, and a frontier model reviews what they record and report. On WorldAuditBench, our auditor succeeds on 55.9% of 213 tasks in Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js worlds, 13.6 points above the strongest auditor reported, at less than a quarter of its cost. It matches the frontier reviewer exploring on its own at 4.6 times lower cost and about half the latency. Without further training, it also answers embodied questions about real-world scans, matching the frontier reviewer exploring on its own and surpassing four other frontier models by 6.4 to 16.6 points.

title: Dynamics of Protected State Evolution

payload.title: Dynamics of Protected State Evolution
payload.abstract: States with identical protected observations can admit different future interventions. Each transition specifies its successor, response increment, required initial reserve and net consumption. Composing these records in execution order distinguishes protocols with equal net consumption and different initial reserve requirements. At a fixed state, a weighted Gram operator determines the linear response ellipsoid and a quotient identifies directions attainable only through cooperation between blocks. Nonlinear systems with identical complete affine data can have incomparable finite-budget response sets. In regular charts, the first correction to quadratic minimum cost is a covariant cubic form involving the third derivative of cost and the Hessians of protection and response. At singular gates, sequential feasibility depends on the peak reserve along the path. A history-weighted operator detects responses outside the old channel's range closure. Controlled congruence characterizes exact reductions of deterministic labelled dynamics, and a two-cut value identity separates the effect of paid verification from that of subsequent action selection. On Qwen2.5-7B Base, two projected policies preserved 2,048 reference top tokens under a per-position KL ceiling of $2\times10^{-5}$. Over 200 arrivals they recovered 391 of 396 initial rejections. Each yielded over 1,200 times the held-out cross-entropy reduction of historical-channel-only AdamW. Under an expanded 2,560-position contract, fixed continuation and neutral renewal began on the same protected logit fiber in distinct structural strata. Both admitted all 200 subsequent writes. Fixed continuation yielded 1.74 times the held-out loss reduction per unit squared write cost. Renewal had a smaller KL excess on the first candidate tested at every arrival and used fewer full verification scans.

title: COVERAGE-TRACE: Source-Side Counterfactual Tracing for Detecting Omissions in LLM Summaries

payload.title: COVERAGE-TRACE: Source-Side Counterfactual Tracing for Detecting Omissions in LLM Summaries
payload.abstract: Omissions are difficult to verify because missing information leaves no output span to inspect: a summary may be factually supported while still excluding a decision, qualification, quantity, or condition needed to preserve the source's meaning. We introduce COVERAGE-TRACE, a source-side counterfactual framework that evaluates omission as dependence on a designated atomic source fact. It replaces only the target fact with type-matched alternatives, holds the candidate summary fixed, and measures the resulting change in its teacher-forced, length-normalized likelihood. A summary covering the target should respond more strongly than one omitting it, while aggregation across multiple counterfactuals reduces sensitivity to replacement choice. We evaluate COVERAGE-TRACE on 80 matched covered--omitted QMSum pairs spanning several fact types and four open-weight models. Multi-CF achieves 0.764--0.825 AUROC, compared with 0.640 for the strongest evaluated text-only baseline. On Falcon-7B, targeted interventions achieve 0.779 AUROC, whereas shuffling counterfactual assignments reduces performance to 0.533; target deletion is effective while unrelated deletion is not. However, adjustment for meaning-preserving paraphrases reduces AUROC to 0.591--0.624. COVERAGE-TRACE therefore provides a practical, complementary signal of target-specific source--summary dependence, but not a wording-invariant semantic coverage probability. These results establish source-side intervention as a promising approach to omission detection while identifying semantic invariance as the central remaining challenge.

title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study

payload.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
payload.abstract: Agent skills are documents in which experts write down procedural knowledge, and models increasingly maintain them by rewriting them without feedback. Such rewriting could adapt a skill to the model that uses it or erode the expert knowledge that makes it useful, yet how skills evolve under this feedback-free self-evolution has not been studied. We let models rewrite expert skills round after round without any task, run or judgment and run agents built on the same models with the rewritten skills. Our experiments show that the skills lose value rather than improve, as every model we test performs worse with them on every benchmark, by 15 points on average on SkillsBench after thirty rounds. Sampling each model's prior with skills it writes from the topic alone, we find that rewriting pulls skills toward this prior and gives up first the knowledge outside it. Putting this knowledge back recovers much of the lost pass rate, so an expert's skill is valuable largely for what the model does not write on its own. Building on this insight, SkillDiff marks this knowledge in place and raises the pass rate on SkillsBench by 4.8 points on average without feedback or any change to the skill's text. Project repository: https://github.com/LitaoGuo/How-Self-Evolution-Reshapes-Skills.

title: LM-based Personalized Travel Planner

payload.title: LM-based Personalized Travel Planner
payload.abstract: Effective travel planning requires handling multiple information sources, managing constraints, and tailoring recommendations to user preferences. While LLMs have introduced dynamic, context-aware decision-making, single-agent models often struggle with complex multi-step reasoning, constraint adherence, and modular execution. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hierarchical multi-agent framework where a supervising chatbot agent coordinates specialized agents for schedule validation, user query formulation, real-time data retrieval, and constraint-aware itinerary generation. By integrating LLM reasoning, external APIs, and iterative refinement mechanisms based on a deterministic, multi-dimensional scoring framework, our approach ensures adaptability, efficiency, and personalization. Evaluations on the well-known TravelPlanner benchmark demonstrate improvements in Budget Constraint planning by 10\%, wider constraints set-based planning by 25\%, and personalized planning results by 45\%. compared to the ReAct baseline. Our code is available at https://github.com/nimashaklaa/TravelPlanner_Research

title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach

payload.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
payload.abstract: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy. The fine-tuned policy is then deployed on its own. On states where a World Action Model and a Vision-Language-Action model have stalled, naming the next step raises subgoal completion by 4.6x over the unchanged task instruction, and the frozen VLM supplies it from the same camera images the policy sees. After fine-tuning, unassisted success on long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, 9.8 points above fine-tuning on human demonstrations and 7.3 points above fine-tuning on self-collected successes at an equal data budget. With a coach that sees only camera images, it reaches 56.8%, above both baselines. The gain is obtained with the action backbone frozen: language coaching teaches the policy what should happen next, and the skills it already has do the rest.

title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization

payload.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
payload.abstract: A recommendation page is consumed as a whole: the items on it compete for attention and complement one another, so the best page is not simply the individually best items placed side by side. We study whole-page optimization, which selects and orders the items on a page jointly to maximize the score of the page. The number of possible pages grows combinatorially, so good pages must be generated rather than enumerated. Some generative re-ranking methods use the same page-level training signal for every choice in a sampled page. Others imitate target pages built before training, which remain largely fixed as the generator improves. We address both limitations with one local page-level objective, which repeatedly moves the current generator toward pages with higher score. This objective splits exactly into one training target per position, and each target compares candidates at the same partial page by the scores of the complete pages they lead to. Every position therefore learns to choose the item that is better for the whole page, rather than the item that looks best on its own. We call this procedure whole-page policy improvement. On two public datasets, KuaiRand-1K and RL4RS-SeqSlate, which cover multi-objective item selection and constrained ordering, and on an industrial dataset of logged pages, our method outperforms the evaluated generative re-ranking baselines. On a synthetic benchmark with a known optimal page, it also comes closest to the optimum, showing that its improvements come from better whole-page decisions.

title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control

payload.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
payload.abstract: Mobile agents on personal smartphones can affect private data, payments, settings, and the foreground screen. We present MATE (Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution), an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between agent action proposals and device effects without modifying the underlying model. MATE represents each UI primitive as a structured action record that combines the instruction, target app, screen context, primitive, and action fields. Runtime Guardrail (RG) maps this record to an allow, block, or user-approval decision; Predefined Task Routing (PTR) serves recurring requests through verified routes with post-execution screen checks; and a floating interface keeps execution in a compact overlay. On MobileSafetyBench, MATE raises high-risk blocking from 29.7% to 97.0% under GPT-4o. On AndroidWorld, it reduces LLM calls by up to 6x and raises recurring-use task success to 95.7%.

title: Multi-View Relighting with Mergeable Radiance Fields

payload.title: Multi-View Relighting with Mergeable Radiance Fields
payload.abstract: We propose MergeableRF, a method for radiance field relighting through model parameter merging. Given multi-view images of a scene under known basis lights, our goal is to relight the scene by directly combining the parameters of radiance fields trained under these lights. This is motivated by the linearity of light transport: the image under a mixture of lights is the same weighted combination of the images under each light. However, combining the parameters of independently trained radiance fields does not produce the corresponding combination of images. To address this, we represent a scene with shared geometry and a separate appearance network for each basis light. We start these networks from the same initialization and introduce merge-aware training, which teaches their parameter combinations to reproduce the corresponding combinations of images. Given a target HDR environment map, we compute its basis-light coefficients and use them to merge the appearance networks into a single relit model. Our method supports both Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), without material estimation, additional relighting networks, or target-specific optimization. Unlike image-space blending, it requires only one rendering pass per viewpoint. Experiments on synthetic Neural Gaffer objects and real OLATverse captures demonstrate relighting quality competitive with methods trained on the same multi-light observations.

title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?

payload.title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
payload.abstract: Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.

title: Mesh-Free Keypoint Learning for Category-Level 6D Object Pose Estimation

payload.title: Mesh-Free Keypoint Learning for Category-Level 6D Object Pose Estimation
payload.abstract: Category-level 6D pose estimation relates partial RGB-D observations of unseen instances to a canonical frame shared across a category. Object-aware reconstruction helps adaptive keypoints retain the geometry of the visible surface. Common reconstruction targets select observed points by their distance to a registered instance surface. We present MORSEPose, which derives this support directly from standard pose and metric-size annotations. We map observed 3D points to normalized object coordinates and retain those inside a tolerancedilated pose-and-size envelope. This construction is consistent across camera frames and metric scales. When the annotated extent bounds the object surface, the envelope conservatively contains the support of a conventional surface-distance selector. We integrate this target with multi-level RGB-D features, adaptive keypoints, and learnable category context. Experiments on REAL275 and HouseCat6D show that the envelope closely matches surface-based supervision at both point and task levels, remains stable under boundary perturbations and viewpoint changes, and supports competitive category-level pose accuracy across benchmarks.

title: Life-IQA+: Boosting Blind Image Quality Assessment via GCN-enhanced Layer Interaction and Flexible Hierarchical Expert Specialization

payload.title: Life-IQA+: Boosting Blind Image Quality Assessment via GCN-enhanced Layer Interaction and Flexible Hierarchical Expert Specialization
payload.abstract: Blind image quality assessment (BIQA) is essential for evaluating and optimizing visual experience. Existing BIQA methods typically aggregate features from multiple backbone stages without accounting for their unequal contributions to quality prediction. Furthermore, uniformly supervising all experts may constrain their flexibility and limit the diversity of the learned quality representations. To address these issues, we present Life-IQA+, a quality representation decoding framework that combines graph convolutional network (GCN) enhanced layer interaction and flexible hierarchical expert specialization. Specifically, the layer interaction module constructs quality queries from GCN-refined deepest-stage features and uses penultimate-stage features as keys and values, thereby enabling cross-layer representation interaction via the cross-attention mechanism. Building on these representations, we further introduce a flexible hierarchical mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture comprising a densely activated shared expert layer and a sparsely activated routed expert layer. To enhance the representation diversity and ability of experts, we apply auxiliary classification supervision to a subset of shared experts using distortion-type labels for synthetic datasets and discretized quality-level labels for authentic datasets. Experiments on synthetic and authentic distortion benchmarks, together with controlled ablations of expert configurations and supervision strategies, show that Life-IQA+ achieves competitive prediction accuracy with a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost. The code is available at: https://github.com/TANGLONG2/Life-IQA-PlusPlus.

title: Carry the Fine Print: Budget-Aware Visual Token Compression for Document OCR

payload.title: Carry the Fine Print: Budget-Aware Visual Token Compression for Document OCR
payload.abstract: Visual token compression often treats salience or similarity as a proxy for transcription importance. Complete document OCR breaks this assumption: small symbols and repeated entries can be indispensable to the transcript despite being visually inconspicuous. We present Select and Compensate, a two-stage framework built on a simple idea: choosing where to retain a token need not determine all the evidence it carries. Selection combines adaptive encoding resolution with global importance and local contrast to choose which tokens to retain as anchors. Compensation enriches these anchors with nearby discarded content and its relative position, without adding tokens. The OCR backbone remains frozen, and native coordinates and structural tokens are preserved. We evaluate complete page transcription across five backbones on OmniDocBench and document reconstruction on MPDocBench. With half the original visual tokens, our input-adapted configuration reaches 95.42 OmniDocBench Overall on Ovis versus 96.09 for the uncompressed model, and paired evaluations show gains over simply reducing the input resolution on both benchmarks. With the original input grid, our method stays within 0.17 points of the uncompressed model at 75% retention and exceeds a learned global selector by 4.70 points at 25%. On a fixed 200-page Ovis workload at the same 50% visual-token budget, only 3 of its outputs hit the length limit, versus 30-34 for the evaluated RTPrune, DivPrune, and HiPrune adaptations, and it finishes the batch 35-40% sooner. Code will be made publicly available.

title: Joint Language Modeling for In-the-Wild Speech-Scene Generation with Distinct Token Representations

payload.title: Joint Language Modeling for In-the-Wild Speech-Scene Generation with Distinct Token Representations
payload.abstract: Speech-scene generation aims to synthesize intelligible target speech together with diverse environmental sounds as a coherent acoustic scene. The task is considered challenging in two respects. Speech and environmental audio differ substantially in their semantic and acoustic characteristics, yet existing approaches typically model the complete scene using a single mixed acoustic representation. At the same time, the two sounds are closely related in real-world speech scenes, whereas conventional approaches usually rely on simulated scenes mixed from independently recorded sources. We propose a large language model (LLM)-based framework for joint modeling of distinct speech and environment token streams. A source-aware neural audio codec extracts temporally aligned speech and environment tokens from mixed audio, and a pretrained LLM generates both token streams in an interleaved fashion conditioned on the natural-language scene description and speech content. This formulation preserves source-specific representations while modeling the token streams within a shared generative context. Since both streams are extracted directly from mixed recordings, the model can also be adapted to in-the-wild speech scenes without isolated sources. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves speech intelligibility, scene relevance, and audio quality over existing speech-scene generation techniques, with consistent gains from real-world adaptation. We further investigate the effects of distinct token representations and interleaved generation, and analyze whether the environmental sound remains stable while speech is active and how the two streams interact.

title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research

payload.title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
payload.abstract: This study proposes a methodological framework for the coordinated use of multiple large language models in academic research. Its central argument is that involving more models does not in itself guarantee more reliable results; what matters is how cognitive and verification operations are organised. The framework is based on seven principles (procedural independence, functional allocation, the diagnostic value of divergence, the diagnostic value of convergence, external verification, proportionality of checking, and human epistemic responsibility) and sets out a non-linear multi-LLM protocol in which independently obtained results are compared, critically examined and, where necessary, verified against external sources. The approach is illustrated through real-world cases drawn from research practice. The study concludes that moving from a single language model to a coordinated multi-LLM process represents a change in the organisation of research, in which the researcher makes the final decisions and bears scholarly responsibility.

title: PRIO: Pre-trained Representation for Interactive Objects in 4D Worlds

payload.title: PRIO: Pre-trained Representation for Interactive Objects in 4D Worlds
payload.abstract: 3D worlds can now be captured, reconstructed, and generated at scale, yet the objects in them stay still: a pressed pillow does not compress, and a pulled door does not swing. Bringing these objects into interactive 4D world models requires a representation of how they can move, deform, and respond physically to user actions in real time. We present PRIO, a pre-trained representation for interactive objects. Given static geometry, PRIO predicts an object-specific configuration space in a single forward pass. This space provides generalized coordinates for Lagrangian mechanics, allowing physical laws and user actions to govern motion. Configurations are linear in these coordinates, allowing the quantities needed by the dynamics to be precomputed. Dynamics then run at interactive rates without further network inference. Pre-trained on diverse 4D trajectories, PRIO learns priors over object configurations that generalize to unseen shapes. It supports meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians, bringing objects in reconstructed and generated scenes into interaction. We demonstrate its use in real-to-sim workflows and robot manipulation. In addition, compared with existing 4D generation methods, PRIO generates dynamics faster and follows user actions more faithfully.

title: Virtual reality and tablet cognitive training improve attention and academic skills without dose effects.

payload.title: Virtual reality and tablet cognitive training improve attention and academic skills without dose effects.
payload.abstract: We evaluated the effects of a closed-loop video game intervention on cognitive and academic outcomes delivered in virtual reality (VR) and tablet formats at two different dosages in a school-based setting. This randomized controlled trial included 158 children aged 8-9 years who completed 30 training sessions over 10 weeks. Compared with an expectancy-matched active control group, both VR and tablet training improved objective measures of attention, including performance-based attention and eye-tracking outcomes. Teacher-rated inattention showed nominal improvement relative to the control group but did not remain statistically significant following correction for multiple comparisons. However, the intervention did not significantly surpass the active control condition for reading or math fluency improvements, indicating no between-group academic advantage. Both VR and tablet versions of the intervention produced comparable outcomes across most measures, with a platform-specific advantage for VR observed only on the performance-based attention measure. Intervention dose did not significantly moderate outcomes, suggesting that efficacy may depend more on achieving sufficient engagement than on total duration. These findings support the use of digital cognitive training to enhance objective measures of attention in school settings, while highlighting the importance of cautious interpretation of academic outcomes in the presence of an active control. (Trial registration: ISRCTN75915439; https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN75915439 ).

title: Systematic review and meta analysis of self guided virtual reality exposure therapy for social anxiety.

payload.title: Systematic review and meta analysis of self guided virtual reality exposure therapy for social anxiety.
payload.abstract: Self-guided virtual reality exposure therapy (SGVRET) may offer a scalable approach for social anxiety, but its independent effects remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with PRISMA and Cochrane methodological guidance. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus, and 13 randomized controlled trials were included. Results indicate that SGVRET was associated with a significant reduction in public speaking anxiety (PSAS; SMD = -1.47, 95% CI [-2.56, -0.37]). For overall social anxiety severity (LSAS/LSAS-SR), the pooled estimate favored SGVRET but did not reach statistical significance and showed substantial heterogeneity (SMD = -0.69, 95% CI [-1.50, 0.13]). No statistically significant improvements were detected for social phobia symptoms (SPS/SPS-6; SMD = -0.17, 95% CI [-0.67, 0.32]) or social interaction anxiety (SIAS/SIAS-6; SMD = -0.35, 95% CI [-1.07, 0.37]). However, most included trials had a high risk of bias, limiting the robustness of the evidence. Overall, the findings suggest that SGVRET may hold potential for performance-related social anxiety, particularly public speaking anxiety, but the current evidence remains preliminary and requires confirmation in larger, rigorous trials.

title: Knowledge graphs for polypharmacy: A systematic review and critical appraisal of reporting quality.

payload.title: Knowledge graphs for polypharmacy: A systematic review and critical appraisal of reporting quality.
payload.abstract: Ensuring medication safety for patients with multi-morbidity, who are often prescribed multiple drugs concomitantly (i.e., polypharmacy), is challenging due to the high risk of drug-drug interactions (DDIs) and accumulation of side-effects. Leveraging large datasets in the form of Knowledge Graphs (KGs) can improve knowledge on drug safety by modeling complex relationships among biomedical entities such as drugs, diseases, proteins and side effects, allowing for the prediction of novel relations. However, it remains unclear to what extent existing KGs adequately capture the polypharmacy context. Therefore, this systematic review identifies KGs constructed and/or utilized for predicting side effects and DDIs in the polypharmacy context, and evaluates their reporting quality. Publications were identified through a structured search through DBLP, MEDLINE, and the ACM Guide to Computing Literature up to January 2026, and supplemented by snowballing. We included peer-reviewed papers presenting KGs developed for and/or used in the context of polypharmacy-related predictions and containing polypharmacy knowledge. We excluded KGs missing both data and code. We adapted and extended a KG evaluation framework to objectively assess the reporting quality of KGs through a review of their documentation from both a technical and a medical domain-specific perspective. Ten studies were included following full-text screening. We provide an overview of relevant statistics, contents, and limitations using our KG evaluation framework. Our study revealed inconsistent technical documentation on KG construction and KG metadata, as well as a lack of knowledge on granular pharmacogenetics and (patho)physiological pathways within the included KGs. Our results show a need for improved quality of reporting, and the incorporation of fine-grained knowledge on pharmacogenetics and (patho)physiological pathways to ensure the long-term re-usability and relevance of KGs in the context of polypharmacy-related predictions. We also recommend to involve medical experts in KG development in this domain.

title: The proposed reform of the Medical Device Regulation and its implications for AI-enabled medical devices in the EU.

payload.title: The proposed reform of the Medical Device Regulation and its implications for AI-enabled medical devices in the EU.
payload.abstract: The European Medical Device Regulations have been criticized for imposing disproportionate barriers to innovation due to excessive regulatory requirements. In response, the European Commission proposed amendments to key regulations in December 2025. The reforms aim to eliminate double regulation, reduce documentation requirements, and introduce new regulatory tools. In this Comment, we argue that these changes are generally well-targeted but leave specific challenges for innovative artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices unresolved.

title: AI chatbots and youth suicide risk: current evidence, critical gaps, and a clinical research agenda.

payload.title: AI chatbots and youth suicide risk: current evidence, critical gaps, and a clinical research agenda.
payload.abstract: Generative AI chatbots are increasingly used by youth for mental health support, but their safety for managing youth suicide risk remains poorly understood. In this paper, we review research on how general-purpose chatbots and AI companions detect and respond to suicide risk disclosures, finding that existing studies rely almost entirely on single-turn, researcher-generated prompts that are not designed with youth in mind. Chatbot performance degrades substantially with indirect, ambiguous, or gradually disclosed risk, which are patterns characteristic of adolescent communication, and the real-world impact of chatbot interactions on youth suicide risk remains unknown. We propose a youth-focused clinical research agenda to address these gaps, organized around four priorities: understanding and integrating youth perspectives through qualitative and participatory research; improving youth-specific risk detection and evaluation methods; examining real-world impacts of chatbot use among youth through prospective outcome research; and improving connection of at-risk youth to crisis resources and trusted adults. Progress will require multidisciplinary collaboration and must evolve alongside rapidly changing chatbot capabilities.

title: Occupational Radiation Effects on Ocular Structures and Visual Function: A Comprehensive Review

payload.title: Occupational Radiation Effects on Ocular Structures and Visual Function: A Comprehensive Review
payload.abstract: Occupational radiation exposure can affect ocular health across medical, nuclear, aviation, outdoor, welding, and other specialized workplace settings. This narrative review is primarily focused on occupational ocular radiation injury and occupational eye protection. It prioritizes human occupational evidence on ionizing radiation and occupationally relevant non-ionizing optical hazards, particularly solar ultraviolet exposure, welding, and lasers, while using experimental or non-occupational evidence only when needed to clarify mechanisms or areas of uncertainty. Evidence is strongest for an association between occupational ionizing radiation and crystalline lens opacity or cataract, whereas evidence for routine occupational effects on the retina, optic nerve, or macula is substantially weaker. Prevention and surveillance are considered using exposure-specific protection frameworks rather than a single radiation model. Psychosocial, quality of life, and economic consequences are treated as secondary downstream implications of visual impairment rather than as evidence of radiation causality.

title: Discordance Between Eye-Specific Clinical Outcomes and Patient-Reported Visual Function After Faricimab Treatment for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Two-Case Report

payload.title: Discordance Between Eye-Specific Clinical Outcomes and Patient-Reported Visual Function After Faricimab Treatment for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Two-Case Report
payload.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration is a retinal disease of older adults causing central vision loss associated with macular neovascularization. Treatment response is commonly evaluated using visual acuity and retinal morphology. These measures may not fully reflect patient-perceived benefit. We report two older adults with neovascular age-related macular degeneration treated with faricimab who demonstrated discordance between clinical and patient-reported outcomes. In the first case, best-corrected visual acuity changed from 20/200 to 20/180 and central retinal thickness decreased from 480 to 389 µm, whereas the National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire–25 score increased from 33.87 to 60.99 and the exploratory ordinal colour-vividness rating was 25 at baseline and 100 at follow-up. In the second case, best-corrected visual acuity improved from 20/100 to 20/45 and central retinal thickness decreased from 341 to 186 µm, whereas the National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire–25 score declined from 67.08 to 33.17 and the exploratory ordinal colour-vividness rating was 75 at baseline and 25 at follow-up. Changes in patient-reported visual functioning may not always parallel conventional clinical outcomes, while the contrasting exploratory colour-vividness ratings observed in these two cases warrant further investigation.

title: Drawing and Soccer Tactical Memorization: An Eye-Tracking Investigation of the Moderating Role of Visuospatial Abilities and Expertise

payload.title: Drawing and Soccer Tactical Memorization: An Eye-Tracking Investigation of the Moderating Role of Visuospatial Abilities and Expertise
payload.abstract: Dynamic drawing has emerged as a strategy to communicate tactical diagrams, yet its effectiveness remains uncertain and appears to depend on individual differences. This study investigated how the memorization and visual processing of tactical soccer scenes are influenced by drawing format (static drawing vs. dynamic drawing) and moderated by visuospatial abilities (VSA) and expertise. Expert (N = 57) and novice (N = 54) participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. In the static drawing condition, participants viewed a pre-drawn, completed tactical diagram accompanied by an oral explanation. In the dynamic drawing condition, they observed the coach drawing the diagram in real time while delivering the same explanation. VSA was first assessed using a control test. Then, in the main test, participants memorized and reproduced the tactical scene while their eye movements were recorded using an eye tracker. Key findings revealed a three-way interaction, highlighting the occurrence of an expertise reversal effect: high VSA novices performed better with dynamic drawing, whereas low VSA experts benefited more from static drawing, showing distinct visual processing patterns across groups. Overall, the results highlight the need to tailor drawing strategies to individual characteristics, particularly VSA and expertise, to optimize visual attention and tactical memorization.

title: Refractive and Vector Outcomes of SMILE Pro with the VISUMAX 800 for High Astigmatism

payload.title: Refractive and Vector Outcomes of SMILE Pro with the VISUMAX 800 for High Astigmatism
payload.abstract: Background/Objectives: High astigmatism remains challenging in keratorefractive lenticule extraction because small errors in centration or cyclotorsion may affect astigmatic correction. This study evaluated early refractive and astigmatic vector outcomes after small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) Pro using the VISUMAX 800 in eyes with high astigmatism. Methods: This prospective interventional cohort study was conducted at Cung Hong Son International Eye Hospital, Hanoi, Vietnam. Refractive outcomes, including uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), manifest refraction, astigmatic vector analysis, and intraoperative and postoperative complications, were evaluated up to 3 months postoperatively. Results: A total of 160 eyes from 102 patients were included in the final analysis. The mean age was 23.7 ± 4.7 years, and 63.7% of participants were female. The mean preoperative spherical equivalent (SEQ) was −7.21 ± 2.03 D, and the mean preoperative refractive cylinder was −2.51 ± 0.56 D. Mean postoperative SEQ was −0.10 ± 0.38 D at 1 month and 0.02 ± 0.31 D at 3 months. At 3 months, 99% and 84% of eyes achieved UDVA of 0.8 decimal or better and 0.9 decimal or better, respectively. The mean residual refractive cylinder was −0.52 ± 0.28 D, with 69% and 98% of eyes achieving a residual cylinder ≤0.50 D and ≤1.00 D, respectively. All eyes had an angle of error within ±15°. The safety index was 1.01, and no eyes lost two or more lines of CDVA. Conclusions: SMILE Pro performed with the VISUMAX 800 provided favorable early 3-month refractive and astigmatic vector outcomes with a satisfactory safety profile in eyes with high astigmatism.

title: Demographic Disparities in AI-Generated Versus Search-Engine-Sourced Images of Ophthalmologists: A Cross-Sectional Analysis

payload.title: Demographic Disparities in AI-Generated Versus Search-Engine-Sourced Images of Ophthalmologists: A Cross-Sectional Analysis
payload.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate demographic representation in AI-generated and search-engine-sourced images of North American ophthalmologists, overall and stratified by subspecialty, and compare these with actual demographic data. Methods: This cross-sectional analysis examined 2000 images (1000 AI-generated and 1000 search-engine-sourced) across ten North American ophthalmology subspecialties. Images were sourced from four AI platforms (DALL·E 3, Firefly, Midjourney, Grok-2) and four search engines (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo!). Using a standardized framework, reviewers assessed gender, race, age group, and professional attire. Pearson chi-squared tests were used to compare image sets with actual demographic data from the Association of American Medical Colleges and Canadian Institute for Health Information. Results: AI-generated images depicted 69% men compared to 64% in search-engine-sourced images (p = 0.047), though both were lower than the actual proportion of male ophthalmologists in North America (71–73%, p < 0.001). White individuals were overrepresented in AI-generated images (81%) relative to both search-engine-sourced images (74%, p = 0.001) and actual demographic data (69%, p < 0.001). Younger individuals (under 50 years) were significantly overrepresented in both image sets, with 82% in AI-generated images and 73% in search-engine-sourced images, compared to only 45–46% in actual demographic data (p < 0.001 for both). AI-generated images also depicted ophthalmologists with significantly more stereotypical medical accessories, including stethoscopes (17% vs. 2%, p < 0.001), glasses (45% vs. 30%, p < 0.001), and white coats (68% vs. 53%, p < 0.001), compared to search-engine-sourced images. Conclusions: AI-generated images diverge from actual demographics, presenting a younger, more stereotypical workforce that paradoxically aligns closer to gender parity than reality.

title: EXPLORING TEACHERS’ PERCEPTION OF SUGGESTING ANGLOMANIACY IN TEACHING ENGLISH TO YOUNG LEARNERS

payload.title: EXPLORING TEACHERS’ PERCEPTION OF SUGGESTING ANGLOMANIACY IN TEACHING ENGLISH TO YOUNG LEARNERS
payload.abstract: Teaching English to young learners generates many benefits, because children have a special capability to learn new knowledge effortlessly. However, teaching them could be challenging with unsupported equipment. This research aims to explore the utilization of a digital tool, Anglomaniacy, in young learner classrooms from the teachers’ perspective, to determine whether it can serve as a supporting tool that enhances learners’ English proficiency skills, such as vocabulary, pronunciation, speaking, reading, and others. This research was conducted online with three teachers from three primary grades in the Indonesia Teaching Community (ITC). The teachers were observed and asked to complete a questionnaire regarding their experience with utilizing Anglomaniacy in their classrooms. Thus, the data were collected through observations and a questionnaire created with Google Forms and shared via WhatsApp. Furthermore, the data of this phenomenological study were analyzed by applying Cresswell’s steps, including transcribing and coding the data. The findings showed that the three teachers suggest that Anglomaniacy has many benefits for teaching English to young learners, including providing useful features, boosting engagement, and vocabulary enhancement. However, they also explain several limitations while using it, such as limited topics and technical issues. Therefore, this research highlights further studies regarding Anglomaniacy use in Indonesia’s curriculum design.

title: Visual Field Loss and Self-Reported Driving Restriction in Glaucoma

payload.title: Visual Field Loss and Self-Reported Driving Restriction in Glaucoma
payload.abstract: Background: To evaluate the association between glaucomatous visual field loss and self-reported driving limitation, and to explore potential threshold ranges of visual field loss associated with an increased likelihood of driving restriction. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 100 patients with primary open-angle glaucoma underwent standard automated perimetry. Visual function was assessed using Mean Deviation (MD) and Visual Field Index (VFI) from the better eye. Driving status, driving limitation, and self-reported driving difficulties were assessed using a structured questionnaire. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to determine independent associations between visual field parameters and driving limitation, adjusting for age, sex, cataract status, and systemic comorbidities. Because MD and VFI are closely related indices of visual field loss, separate multivariable models were constructed for each parameter. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to explore threshold values associated with driving limitation. Results: Driving limitation increased progressively with worsening functional severity, affecting 17% of participants with preserved function, 48% of those with borderline impairment, and 72% of those with definite impairment (p < 0.001). Reduced VFI was independently associated with driving limitation (OR = 0.972, 95% CI: 0.948–0.996; p = 0.021). In a separate model, more negative MD was also independently associated with driving limitation (OR = 0.924, 95% CI: 0.875–0.976; p = 0.004). Male sex was associated with a lower likelihood of driving limitation. ROC analysis identified threshold values of VFI ≤ 71% (AUC = 0.663) and MD ≤ −13.36 dB (AUC = 0.650), both characterized by high specificity but limited sensitivity. Participants who had ceased driving demonstrated worse visual field indices than active drivers, whereas never-drivers showed no consistent association with visual field loss. Conclusions: Glaucomatous visual field loss was significantly associated with self-reported driving limitation and behavioural self-regulation. Objective perimetric parameters, particularly VFI and MD in the better eye, may help identify patients more likely to report driving difficulties. The reported threshold values should be interpreted as exploratory reference points rather than clinically actionable criteria and require further validation before clinical application.

title: Longitudinal Retinal Layer Changes After Deep Sclerectomy in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Three-Year Retrospective Cohort Study Using Spectral-Domain OCT

payload.title: Longitudinal Retinal Layer Changes After Deep Sclerectomy in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Three-Year Retrospective Cohort Study Using Spectral-Domain OCT
payload.abstract: Background: To evaluate longitudinal peripapillary and macular retinal layer changes over three years before and after deep sclerectomy (DS) in eyes with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods: This retrospective monocentric study included 150 eyes undergoing DS with intraoperative mitomycin C. Cohort 1 (n = 111) was analyzed for absolute retinal layer thickness changes and cohort 2 (n = 39) for pre- and postoperative thinning rates using spectral-domain OCT. Intraocular pressure (IOP), medication use, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and visual field mean defect (MD) were assessed over three years. Results: Mean IOP decreased significantly at three years in both cohorts (cohort 1: 22.8 ± 0.7 to 14.9 ± 0.7 mmHg; cohort 2: 20.8 ± 1.2 to 13.5 ± 0.9 mmHg; both p < 0.001), alongside a significant reduction in medication use (p < 0.001). BCVA remained stable, whereas MD worsened significantly in a mixed-effects model (cohort 1: +0.70 dB/year, p = 0.002; cohort 2: +0.74 dB/year, p < 0.001). Despite sustained IOP reduction, mean peripapillary RNFL thickness declined (cohort 1: 60.1 ± 1.4 to 56.6 ± 1.8 µm, p < 0.001; cohort 2: 61.1 ± 2.4 to 57.4 ± 2.9 µm, p = 0.005). In cohort 2, the macular RNFL thinning rate decreased numerically after surgery (−1.40 ± 0.67 to −0.08 ± 0.47 µm/year; difference 1.32 µm/year, 95% CI −0.28 to 2.92; p = 0.11). Macular layers showed no significant changes. Conclusions: DS achieved sustained IOP reduction with stable visual acuity, but visual field MD worsened over three years. Peripapillary RNFL thinning persisted postoperatively, though macular thinning rates showed a non-significant reduction. Structural monitoring remains necessary after glaucoma surgery despite adequate IOP control.

title: Global Ophthalmology Research Output Relative to Disease Burden and National Income, 2011–2021

payload.title: Global Ophthalmology Research Output Relative to Disease Burden and National Income, 2011–2021
payload.abstract: Purpose: To characterize ophthalmology research output relative to disease burden and national economic capacity after accounting for population size. Methods: We analyzed Scopus publications, Global Burden of Disease disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and World Bank economic and population data from 2011 to 2021. Negative binomial and Gamma models evaluated publication volume and positive citation-weighted impact, adjusting for DALYs, gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, population, disease category, and publication year. Results: Refractive disorders accounted for 45.4% of DALYs and 23.2% of publication volume; cataract, 44.7% and 29.8%; glaucoma, 5.2% and 30.6%; and age-related macular degeneration, 3.8% and 15.2%. High-income countries accounted for 11.8% of burden, 67.2% of publication volume, and 74.2% of citation-weighted impact; lower-middle-income countries accounted for 49.1%, 7.9%, and 6.8%, respectively. DALYs were not independently associated with publication volume (adjusted count ratio [aCR], 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.98–1.01; p = 0.278), whereas GDP per capita (aCR, 4.47) and population (aCR, 13.99) were strongly associated (both p < 0.001). For positive citation-weighted impact, DALYs had a small association (adjusted ratio of means [aRM], 1.05), whereas GDP per capita (aRM, 2.86) and population (aRM, 4.96) were strongly associated (all p < 0.001). Conclusions: After accounting for population size, absolute disease burden was not independently associated with publication volume, whereas national economic capacity remained strongly associated with both outcomes. These patterns should inform research and service-delivery priorities.

title: Seeing Inequalities: Self-Reported Visual Difficulty and Eye Care Utilization Among Women in Malawi, a Secondary Analysis of the 2024 Demographic and Health Survey Data

payload.title: Seeing Inequalities: Self-Reported Visual Difficulty and Eye Care Utilization Among Women in Malawi, a Secondary Analysis of the 2024 Demographic and Health Survey Data
payload.abstract: Background: This study aimed to identify the factors associated with self-reported visual difficulty and uptake of spectacle/contact lens correction among women of reproductive age in Malawi. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2024 Malawi Demographic and Health Survey data. Outcomes were self-reported visual difficulty and use of spectacles/contact lenses. Age, residence, region, education, and marital status were examined as associated variables. Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages. Chi-square tests, multinomial and binary logistic regression models were used to assess associations. Results: The analysis included 5634 women aged 15–49 years; 78.3% lived in rural areas, and 62.4% had primary education. Self-reported visual difficulty was significantly associated with region, age, residence, education, and marital status (all p ≤ 0.004). Reported use of spectacle/contact lenses was also associated with these factors. Increasing age was associated with higher odds of reporting “some difficulty” seeing (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.06–1.09). Compared with women in the Southern region, those from the Northern (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.5–2.9) and Central regions (OR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2–2.1) had higher odds of reporting visual difficulty, with stronger associations for “a lot of difficulty” in the Central region (OR 4.3, 95% CI 2.1–8.6). Urban residence was associated with higher odds whereas being married/living together, divorced/separated, or widowed was associated with lower odds. Conclusion: Self-reported visual difficulty and use of spectacles/contact lenses varied by demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Targeted strategies to improve access to affordable eye care may reduce barriers to uptake of corrective services and reduce visual impairment among women in Malawi.

title: DESIGNING PUPPET-BASED ENGLISH LEARNING VIDEOS FOR FOURTH GRADERS: A NEEDS-DRIVEN DEVELOPMENT STUDY

payload.title: DESIGNING PUPPET-BASED ENGLISH LEARNING VIDEOS FOR FOURTH GRADERS: A NEEDS-DRIVEN DEVELOPMENT STUDY
payload.abstract: English learning at the elementary level requires engaging instructional media to support vocabulary and speaking development. However, the systematic integration of needs analysis into puppet-based video design remains underexplored in Indonesian EFL contexts. This study aimed to develop a puppet-based English learning video for fourth-grade students and to evaluate its validity and feasibility through expert judgment. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) design based on the Analysis, Design, and Development phases of the ADDIE model. Data were collected from 20 fourth-grade students and two English teachers using questionnaires grounded in needs analysis principles. The findings revealed that students prioritized speaking skills (55%), experienced difficulties in vocabulary retention, and preferred video-based (65%) and puppet-assisted (85%) learning media. Based on these findings, a seven-minute puppet-based instructional video entitled "My Day with Kiko" was developed. The prototype was validated by one independent expert in English Education across content and media presentation aspects, achieving an overall mean score of 3.79 out of 4.00 (material: 4.00, media: 3.57), categorized as very valid and feasible. The study concludes that needs-driven instructional development can produce pedagogically appropriate multimedia resources for young EFL learners. Future research is recommended to examine its effectiveness through classroom implementation.

title: Short-Term Residual Myopic Bias Measured by Open-Field Autorefraction After 10-Second Myopic Overcorrection in Young Myopic Adults

payload.title: Short-Term Residual Myopic Bias Measured by Open-Field Autorefraction After 10-Second Myopic Overcorrection in Young Myopic Adults
payload.abstract: The magnitude and short-term recovery of residual objective myopic bias after a brief, clinically plausible over-minus exposure during distance refraction remain insufficiently quantified. This study quantified the short-term residual objective myopic shift following 10 s of transient myopic overcorrection of 0.50 D or 1.00 D in young adults with myopia. Twenty healthy young adults with myopia and low astigmatism underwent open-field automated objective over-refraction (OR) while viewing a high-contrast 5 m target. After trial lenses induced a moderate myopic state, each participant completed three randomized 10 s lens conditions: 0.50 D undercorrection, 0.50 D overcorrection, and 1.00 D overcorrection. The primary endpoint was OR at 5 s after restoration of the objective neutral correction. Both overcorrection conditions produced significantly more negative OR than undercorrection at 5 s; exploratory analyses showed the same pattern at 10 s. The shift was evident at 5 and 10 s after restoration of the objective neutral correction and, by 30 s, was no longer statistically significant and appeared clinically negligible. This bias should be considered when OR measurements obtained shortly after over-minus lens exposure are used to inform subsequent subjective refinement.

title: Oculomotor Dance Task: Implications for Audio–Visual-Cued Spatial Learning

payload.title: Oculomotor Dance Task: Implications for Audio–Visual-Cued Spatial Learning
payload.abstract: This study aims to address whether a new visual–motor-based learning paradigm with music can potentially promote neuroplasticity and create new interventional tools, building upon prior research that shows behavioral and putative neural changes following dance-based neurorehabilitation in people with Parkinson’s disease (PD). Eye movements of 10 healthy adult participants, aged 20–25, were tracked using the Eyelink 1000 Plus system during a 68 s eye dance sequence. The experiment consisted of a learning phase, where participants observed the sequence five times with 30 s breaks, and a performance phase, where they performed the sequence five times from memory on a gray screen without visual cues. Results showed a significant improvement in percentage of total movements performed correctly between the first session (g1; M = 40%, SD = 7.2%) and the last session (g5; M = 69.7%, SD = 22.8%). Similarly, there was significant improvement in the average time on beat from the intended choreography timing, between the first session (g1; M = 0.29, SD = 0.06) and the fifth session (g5; M = 0.46, SD = 0.12). These findings suggest that eye movement choreography has the potential to be learned within healthy adults.

title: Real-World Comparison of Overall Survival Among Patients With and Without Inherited Retinal Diseases

payload.title: Real-World Comparison of Overall Survival Among Patients With and Without Inherited Retinal Diseases
payload.abstract: This study compared real-world overall survival and the risk of physical comorbidities and mental health conditions among patients aged <65 years with versus without inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) in the United States (US). Optum® Electronic Health Record data (January 2014–January 2023) were evaluated for IRD (patients with ≥2 medical visits with an IRD diagnosis; index date: second such medical visit) and non-IRD (patients without an IRD diagnosis; index date: random medical visit) cohorts. Baseline demographics were balanced between cohorts using propensity score matching (2:1). Outcome measures were overall survival (date of death due to any cause) and presence of physical comorbidities and mental health conditions (medical visit with a corresponding diagnosis code). In total, 4594 patients with IRD were matched to 9188 patients without IRD (mean age: 38.7 vs. 38.2 years, 53.9% vs. 55.1% female, mean follow-up: 53.1 vs. 52.8 months). Over 84 months, patients with versus without IRD had a 24% higher risk of death (overall survival: 95.8% vs. 96.7%; hazard ratio: 1.24; 95% confidence interval: 1.00–1.53; p = 0.046) and were at significantly higher risk for each evaluated physical comorbidity and mental health condition (all p < 0.05). The development of novel therapies is thus needed to address the clinical burden of IRD.

title: Association of Preoperative Personality Traits with Six-Month Subjective Quality of Vision After Bilateral PanOptix Trifocal IOL Implantation: A Prospective Single-Center Study

payload.title: Association of Preoperative Personality Traits with Six-Month Subjective Quality of Vision After Bilateral PanOptix Trifocal IOL Implantation: A Prospective Single-Center Study
payload.abstract: Purpose: To investigate the association between preoperative personality traits and subjective quality of vision six months after bilateral trifocal intraocular lens (IOL) implantation. Methods: This prospective, single-center study included 66 patients undergoing bilateral implantation of the AcrySof IQ PanOptix TFNT00 trifocal IOL. Personality traits were assessed preoperatively using the Mini-International Personality Item Pool (Mini-IPIP). Six months after surgery, participants completed the Quality of Vision (QoV) questionnaire. Associations between the five personality dimensions and global QoV score, as well as individual visual symptoms, were evaluated. Results: Postoperative visual acuity was good at all distances (mean binocular uncorrected visual acuity: 0.04 ± 0.05 logMAR at distance, 0.06 ± 0.05 logMAR at intermediate, and 0.08 ± 0.05 logMAR at near). All five personality dimensions were significantly associated with global QoV scores (all pFDR < 0.05): extraversion (ρ = −0.343), agreeableness (ρ = −0.378), conscientiousness (ρ = −0.344), and openness to experience (ρ = −0.318) were associated with better subjective quality of vision, whereas neuroticism was associated with worse QoV (ρ = 0.428). Neuroticism showed the strongest correlation with starburst perception (ρ = 0.603, p < 0.001), while agreeableness demonstrated the strongest negative association with blurred vision (ρ = −0.524, p < 0.001). Halo, glare, starburst, hazy vision, blurred vision, and fluctuation in vision were consistently associated with multiple personality dimensions. Conclusions: Personality traits are significantly associated with patients’ subjective perception of visual quality following bilateral trifocal IOL implantation. Assessing personality before surgery may help identify patients at greater risk of postoperative dissatisfaction and guide more personalized counseling for those considering premium intraocular lenses.

title: INDONESIAN EFL STUDENTS' PERCEPTIONS AND CHALLENGES IN DEVELOPING ACADEMIC LISTENING COMPETENCE: A MIXED-METHOD INVESTIGATION

payload.title: INDONESIAN EFL STUDENTS' PERCEPTIONS AND CHALLENGES IN DEVELOPING ACADEMIC LISTENING COMPETENCE: A MIXED-METHOD INVESTIGATION
payload.abstract: This research examines how students perceive and understand academic listening, a fundamental skill for success in educational settings. Through questionnaire distribution among secondary and tertiary students, the study identifies common obstacles and approaches students employ when engaging with academic content. Findings reveal that although students acknowledge academic listening's significance, many encounter difficulties processing lecture structures, identifying key information, and maintaining focus during extended listening sessions. The restricted exposure to authentic academic discourse and insufficient training in specialized listening strategies compound these challenges. Recommendations include implementing systematic listening practice, enhancing exposure to genuine academic materials, and incorporating technology-based tools for autonomous skill development.

title: E-MOTE: A Conceptual Framework for Emotion-Aware Teacher Training Integrating FACS, AI and VR

payload.title: E-MOTE: A Conceptual Framework for Emotion-Aware Teacher Training Integrating FACS, AI and VR
payload.abstract: This paper proposes E-MOTE (Emotion-aware Teacher Education Framework), an ethically grounded conceptual model aimed at enhancing teacher education through the integrated use of the Facial Action Coding System (FACS), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Virtual Reality (VR). As a conceptual and design-oriented proposal, E-MOTE is presented as a structured blueprint for future development and empirical validation, not as an implemented or evaluated system. Grounded in neuroscientific and educational research, E-MOTE seeks to strengthen teachers’ emotional awareness, teacher noticing, and social–emotional learning competencies.
